items.title: 吃了褪黑素还是睡不好？ 长期失眠的你 可能走错了第一步 很多人失眠了第一反应就是吃褪黑素，或者尝试放白噪音、睡前不刷手机……结果试了几天发现，该睡不着的还是睡不着。 于是开始怀疑是不是褪黑素不管用，或者其他方法不适合自己。 💡褪黑素本质上是一种调节生物钟的激素，并不是直接催眠的药物。它更适合倒时差、短期作息紊乱等情况。 如果你是压力大、焦虑失眠、或者持续了好几个月，靠褪黑素或者普通催眠方法很难起效

items.abstract: Abstract Background The pathogenic fungi Thielaviopsis punctulata and Thielaviopsis paradoxa cause black scorch disease in date palm ( Phoenix dactylifera L.), relying on secreted cell wall-degrading enzymes (CWDEs) to invade host tissues. To test whether Trichoderma secondary metabolites directly block these enzymes, we docked viridin, harzianic acid, trichodermin, and gliotoxin in silico against two modeled T. punctulata targets: a GH45 cellulase (AlphaFold) and a GH11 xylanase (SWISS-MODEL). Simulations were run in AutoDock Vina (exhaustiveness 32; three random seeds) using the native substrates cellobiose and xylobiose as baselines. Results Viridin and harzianic acid showed the strongest binding in both cellulase (− 8.00 and − 7.80 kcal/mol) and xylanase (− 7.67 and − 7.63 kcal/mol), matching substrate affinities (− 7.23 and − 7.10 kcal/mol) within Vina’s error margin despite slightly lower heavy-atom ligand efficiency. Conformational consistency further separated the top candidates: all 27 harzianic acid poses (9 per seed) localized inside the active-site clefts, with top-ranked orientations contacting both catalytic residues and sharing 46% and 81% spatial overlap with the docked substrates in cellulase and xylanase, respectively. Both trichodermin and gliotoxin bound more weakly (− 6.30 to − 6.80 kcal/mol), often missing one of the two catalytic residues. In SwissADME, we recorded only basic physicochemical descriptors, as its oral drug-likeness rules do not apply to fungal toxins like the other three tested metabolites. Conclusions Although rigid-receptor docking cannot replace molecular dynamics or wet-lab work, our results suggest that harzianic acid, and possibly viridin, could compete with native substrates for CWDE active sites, warranting in vitro enzymatic and fungal growth assays. items.abstract: Abstract Carotid atherosclerosis remains a major contributor to cerebrovascular events, with macrophage-driven inflammation playing a pivotal role in disease progression. This study employed an integrative multi-omics approach combining bulk RNA sequencing and weighted gene correlation network analysis to identify critical differential expression genes in atherogenesis. Machine learning algorithms (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, random forest and artificial neural network) prioritized Toll Like Receptor 1 as the most significant risk gene. Single-cell sequencing of carotid plaques demonstrated TLR1 was predominantly distributed in macrophages. Experimental validation in mouse bone marrow primary macrophages confirmed that coriander inhibits TLR1-mediated macrophage inflammatory response in carotid plaques. Immune infiltration analysis showed that TLR1 was closely related to neutrophil and macrophage activation. Our findings establish TLR1 as a macrophage-specific diagnostic biomarker and suggest that ingestion of coriander supplementation inhibits the inflammatory amplification circuit in TLR1-mediated advanced atherosclerosis.

items.summary: Abstract Background Single-cell genetic variation research has expanded rapidly with advances in sequencing technologies and computational approaches and is increasingly important for investigating cellular heterogeneity, clonal evolution, and disease-associated genomic alterations. However, key methodological and experimental information is often dispersed across full-text publications, limiting systematic…
items.abstract: Abstract Background Single-cell genetic variation research has expanded rapidly with advances in sequencing technologies and computational approaches and is increasingly important for investigating cellular heterogeneity, clonal evolution, and disease-associated genomic alterations. However, key methodological and experimental information is often dispersed across full-text publications, limiting systematic characterization of the field. To address this, we combined large-scale literature analysis with full-text structured information extraction assisted by the large language model (LLM) ChatGPT-4o to characterize technological, methodological, and application trends in single-cell genetic variation research. Results Information on sequencing technologies, variant types, disease applications, species, and variant detection tools was systematically extracted and organized. ChatGPT-4o-assisted extraction achieved a mean correctness of 82.50% and a mean completeness of 83.05% compared with manually curated annotations. Single-cell genetic variation research has expanded rapidly, accompanied by increasing international and institutional collaboration. scRNA-seq remains the predominant technology, while scATAC-seq, scDNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and multi-omics combinations are increasingly adopted. Cancer is the major application area, with tumor microenvironment, prognosis, and immunotherapy as prominent themes. SNVs remain the most extensively studied variant type, whereas combined SNV-CNV analyses are becoming more common, particularly in cancer studies. Bulk-oriented tools such as GATK remain widely used, while single-cell-specific methods are increasingly adopted to address low coverage, allelic dropout, and technical noise. Conclusions Single-cell genetic variation research is evolving toward integrated multi-omics, multi-variant analysis, and more specialized single-cell computational strategies. The increasing adoption of multi-omics technologies and single-cell-specific methods reflects the growing complexity and maturity of the field. Combining large-scale literature analysis with LLM-assisted full-text information extraction provides a systematic approach for capturing complex methodological and biological information and identifying emerging directions in single-cell genomics.

items.abstract: FusionGDB has served diverse biological, health, and clinical research communities as a unique functional annotation knowledgebase of human fusion genes. In this study, we report an updated resource of human fusion gene annotation (FusionGDB 3.0), available at https://compbio.uth.edu/FusionGDB/. FusionGDB 3.0 includes substantial content updates: 156K up-to-date human fusion genes established by integrating 216K RNA-seq-based and 100K WGS-based breakpoint events, comprehensive open reading frame annotations, protein domain retention searches, and 1.13 million personalized fusion protein sequences reflecting individual nsSNVs from TCGA and CCLE, as well as N- and C-truncated protein sequences alongside canonical in-frame products. Furthermore, it incorporates 18K potential tumorigenic scenarios, supported by evidence from the literature, spanning drug-targetable gene group fusions, the epigenomic architecture around breakpoint junctions, and therapeutic prioritization scoring. FusionGDB 3.0 establishes a systematic framework for the functional annotation of coding structural variants. FusionGDB 3.0 serves as a pivotal reference knowledgebase for the genomics, oncology, and precision pharmacology communities, while also functioning as a foundational benchmark dataset for training and validating machine learning models, structural biology platforms, and AI-driven therapeutic discovery pipelines.

items.abstract: Acetamiprid (ACE) has been implicated not only in bone metabolic disorders but also in the development of various cancers. Nevertheless, its role in osteosarcoma (OS) and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. We integrated network toxicology, transcriptomics, molecular docking, single-cell analysis, machine learning, and preliminary in vitro experiments to explore potential links between ACE-related targets and OS-associated signatures. We identified 219 ACE-related targets and 3299 OS-associated genes, including 62 overlapping candidates. Functional enrichment analyses highlighted inflammatory pathways, including TNF and IL-17 signaling. Exploratory machine learning analyses prioritized CAT and MPO, with CAT showing comparatively more consistent support across subsequent analyses and MPO showing less consistent cross-dataset performance. CAT demonstrated dataset-level discriminatory performance in the evaluated public transcriptomic datasets. Immune-context and single-cell analyses further characterized associations between candidate-gene expression, inferred immune-cell composition, and cellular distribution. Molecular docking generated computationally plausible ACE-protein binding poses but did not establish direct target engagement. In vitro, ACE treatment altered cellular metabolic activity, wound closure, and CAT expression in U-2 OS cells under the tested conditions. CAT emerged as a prioritized candidate molecular feature associated with ACE-related cellular responses and OS-associated molecular signatures. These findings are exploratory and do not establish a causal relationship between ACE exposure and OS development or progression. Further studies using independent tissue cohorts, mechanistic gene perturbation, direct target-engagement assays, and in vivo validation are required.

items.abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-M) is a rare but often fatal immune-related adverse event. Large language models (LLMs) have provided new opportunities for patient education, yet whether they can effectively support patient education in ICI-M remains unknown. In this study, we submitted 20 standardized ICI-M-related patient questions to five LLMs (ChatGPT-5.5, Gemini-3.5 Flash, DeepSeek-V4, Qwen 3.7, and Doubao), generating 100 responses. Model performance was evaluated using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), Quality Analysis of Medical Artificial Intelligence (QAMAI), Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP), Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool understandability and actionability scores (PEMAT-U and PEMAT-A), and six readability indices. Significant inter-model differences were observed across most quality and readability metrics, and no single model outperformed the others across all dimensions. DeepSeek-V4 achieved the highest mDISCERN score [5.00 (IQR, 4.00–5.00)], whereas ChatGPT-5.5 achieved the highest PEMAT-A score [40.00 (IQR, 35.00–45.00)]. Readability was suboptimal, with a mean FKGL of 16.60 ± 2.64. Correlation analyses demonstrated information quality, usability, and readability represented correlated but distinct evaluation dimensions. While LLMs may serve as adjunctive tools for ICI-M patient education, substantial optimization of content accessibility and actionability is required prior to clinical implementation.

items.title: DailySafe: Benchmarking Dynamic Safety Awareness in Everyday Multi-Turn Multimodal Interactions
items.summary: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become increasingly integrated into everyday life, their ability to provide safe and reliable assistance in realistic daily activities remains insufficiently explored. Existing safety benchmarks primarily focus on isolated harmful requests or adversarial scenarios, overlooking the safety risks that may arise as ordinary tasks unfold. items.abstract: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become increasingly integrated into everyday life, their ability to provide safe and reliable assistance in realistic daily activities remains insufficiently explored. Existing safety benchmarks primarily focus on isolated harmful requests or adversarial scenarios, overlooking the safety risks that may arise as ordinary tasks unfold. In practice, users pursue legitimate goals through multi-turn, multimodal interactions, where seemingly benign requests may become safety-critical when considered alongside earlier actions and visual observations. This calls for Dynamic Safety Awareness, the ability to track evolving task conditions, recognize implicit contextual risks, and provide safe and helpful assistance. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce DailySafe, a benchmark comprising 195 naturalistic multi-turn, multi-image interactions across 10 everyday domains and 42 task categories. Grounded in authentic user dialogue topics and documented safety knowledge, DailySafe captures realistic scenarios where safety-critical evidence is progressively revealed across conversational turns and visual observations. Using case-specific safety annotations, DailySafe assesses whether MLLMs can recognize and appropriately address evolving risks while supporting users' legitimate goals, bringing multimodal safety evaluation closer to real-world everyday AI assistance. DailySafe is publicly available at: https://github.com/XuankunRong/DailySafe.

items.title: Posterior Matching Distillation
items.summary: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We…
items.abstract: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

items.title: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher
items.summary: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. Even successful teacher trajectories can contain unsupported assumptions, unproductive repetition, or superficial verification. items.abstract: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. Even successful teacher trajectories can contain unsupported assumptions, unproductive repetition, or superficial verification. We propose Skill-FT (Skill-Guided Fine-Tuning), which uses natural-language skills to suppress undesirable habits and elicit underrepresented effective behaviors during teacher rollouts, then fine-tunes a target model on the resulting trajectories. We introduce AutoMaster, an autonomous post-training system in which an LLM agent develops these interventions through trajectory analysis, skill design, data selection, and feedback from rollouts and target-model evaluation. Across Terminal, Search, and software engineering tasks with 4B and 9B target models, AutoMaster improves mean performance over Vanilla SFT on successful unguided teacher trajectories by 1.42-8.99 percentage points, with the teacher, task pool, training set size, and SFT recipe held fixed. Together with the ablations and trajectory analyses, these results suggest that behavioral shaping can make a fixed model a more effective teacher. We further find that retaining skill instructions during SFT yields higher mean performance than removing them across all six settings, despite their absence at evaluation and identical supervised outputs. These findings suggest that preserving skill context as part of a training demonstration can support better behavioral internalization.

items.abstract: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is the stage in which Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs) advance their capability to reason over video. However, the VideoLLM also learns to answer from textual regularities of its training data, a shortcut that bypasses the video. The regularities behind the shortcut are hard to define at the data level, and the shortcut forms regardless of training epoch, data size, or backbone. The shortcut is hidden behind a rise in accuracy within the training distribution, yet it is not required for the rise and even costs SFT the gain the video offers under distribution shift. We therefore propose Video-Evidence Training via Orthogonal projection (VETO), which intervenes on the fine-tuning update where the shortcut is written rather than on the data. VETO calibrates the subspace that the text alone occupies in the activations of the base model and projects the update onto its orthogonal complement. The VideoLLM is thus left to ground its answer in the full input, with the shortcut suppressed as it forms and never defined. Across seven VideoLLMs, VETO preserves the gain of SFT on the training distribution and suppresses the shortcut. On six benchmarks under shift it gains more than SFT and answers from the full input rather than the shortcut. Code is available at https://github.com/Youngwoo-git/VETO.

items.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
items.summary: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. items.abstract: Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.

By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. items.abstract: We present Depth Pro 2, an approach to estimating dense metric depth for images and video at full resolution. By analyzing prior methods for monocular depth estimation, we find that they commonly trade off temporal consistency and boundary sharpness: multi-frame methods favor consistency, single-frame methods favor sharpness. To overcome this trade-off, we train a single, scalable network that processes both images and video and predicts depth maps at native resolution. Depth Pro 2 produces depth maps that are metrically accurate, sharp, and temporally consistent all at once, outperforming prior work in all of these dimensions. We release a family of models that define a new Pareto frontier in terms of metric accuracy, sharpness, temporal consistency, and runtime. We release code and weights at https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-depth-pro-2/

items.title: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
items.summary: Humans act in the visual world by inferring the 3D layout behind a 2D view, predicting how an action changes it, and correcting themselves after seeing the result. Can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) do the same? items.abstract: Humans act in the visual world by inferring the 3D layout behind a 2D view, predicting how an action changes it, and correcting themselves after seeing the result. Can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) do the same? CAPTCHAs offer a natural test, since humans solve them through this very loop, clicking and dragging on the screen and adjusting after each result. Yet existing CAPTCHA benchmarks are largely solved and rarely spatial, while spatial benchmarks rarely require action. We therefore present TuringSpace, a synthetic web environment of 125 interactive CAPTCHAs that span five spatial abilities and must be solved through clicks and drags on the screen. Every task is a program that generates new instances with a checker and an oracle, so the tasks also form a scalable training gym. Humans solve 94.1% of the tasks, whereas the best model, GPT-6 Astra, still fails 25.9% of them, and the best open-weight model, Kimi K3, fails 68.0%. Our further analysis shows that most failures come from misreading the screenshot, and that model reasoning rarely corrects a wrong belief but hallucinates evidence to defend it. To test whether such spatial abilities can be learned, we fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B on this gym. Its success rate rises from 1.6% to 33.1%, above Kimi K3, and it improves on all seven out-of-distribution benchmarks, including a 9.9-point gain on the real-world indoor videos of VSI-Bench. These results show that grounding spatial intelligence in screen actions exposes what MLLMs lack and offers a scalable way to teach it, with gains that transfer to real-world scenes. We will release TuringSpace to support further study.

items.abstract: Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. In this report, we introduce WeMM-Video, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants. Centering on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm, seamlessly supporting both a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses and a thinking mode for explicit step-by-step reasoning. The models are trained on a large-scale multimodal corpus of approximately 1.2 trillion tokens through progressive pre-training and a multi-stage post-training pipeline incorporating multi-teacher OPD, anti-repetition MrDPO, and specialist RL. Evaluated across more than 120 benchmarks, WeMM-Video demonstrates superior performance in omni-modal video understanding and reasoning, while maintaining highly competitive capabilities across general audio, silent video, image, and text tasks. Specifically, in omni-modal video evaluations, our flagship WeMM-Video-35B-A3B establishes a new open-source state of the art, substantially outperforming proprietary models such as Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash and Seed2.0-Mini-0428 while narrowing the gap with the strong Gemini-3.0-Flash, and our compact WeMM-Video-9B surpasses the larger open-source Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct. We publicly release the WeMM-Video family along with our evaluation and reproduction pipeline to foster further research and development in the open-source community.

Existing caption formats also offer limited support for combining detailed narration with precise timing. items.abstract: Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, yet current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misinterpret the wearer's motion. Existing caption formats also offer limited support for combining detailed narration with precise timing. We present EgoCaptioner, which pairs a video-level overview of the setting, participants, and the wearer's overall activity with timed steps whose narration adapts to varying perceptual demands and marks key moments at specific timestamps. We develop a coarse-to-fine annotation pipeline that establishes event structure before expanding step descriptions, yielding 50,000 training examples from eight egocentric video sources. Complementary rewards assess factual accuracy and coverage, measure step-level temporal alignment, and penalize fragmented or redundant narration, guiding caption refinement through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). To improve the reliability of factual supervision, we supplement caption references with pose-derived motion facts when sensor data are available. Across five egocentric benchmarks, EgoCaptioner achieves leading performance among evaluated open-source models in caption quality, caption-conditioned question answering, and temporal alignment. It also surpasses Gemini 3.1 Pro on PhysCapBench and all evaluated proprietary baselines on Minerva-Ego under the caption-to-QA protocol. Ablations support the complementary roles of factual and temporal rewards and show that coarse-to-fine annotation provides more effective supervision than single-pass annotation.

items.title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
items.summary: Code2Video uses agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video generation, enabling explicit control over structure and dynamics. However, how to construct proxies and prompts for optimal downstream quality remains underexplored, as do the capabilities and limitations of this paradigm. Through controlled experiments and blinded human evaluation, we study proxy granularity, physics simulation, and prompting. The results…
items.abstract: Code2Video uses agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video generation, enabling explicit control over structure and dynamics. However, how to construct proxies and prompts for optimal downstream quality remains underexplored, as do the capabilities and limitations of this paradigm. Through controlled experiments and blinded human evaluation, we study proxy granularity, physics simulation, and prompting. The results reveal task-dependent trade-offs: coarse proxies favor natural motion, while medium-grained proxies favor consistency. Physics simulation and proxy-aligned prompting further improve average quality. Guided by these findings, we introduce Coda-DaVinci, a task-adaptive agentic framework for Code2Video generation that selects between proxy-guided and direct generation, adapts modeling granularity to each entity, and coordinates simulation with proxy-grounded prompting. Its multi-agent harness preserves scene assets and guides repairs through visual inspection and independent review. Experiments demonstrate leading instruction following on VTR and scene consistency on R2M, improved physical plausibility over direct generation, and higher visual realism than the compared Code2Video baselines. Long-video evaluations further show gains in event structure and consistency across successive interactions, while revealing limitations in transition stability and adherence to scene settings.

items.abstract: Abstract Purpose Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) relies on planning computed tomography (CT) for dose calculation, which introduces inherent CT/MR registration errors, unnecessary radiation exposure, and suboptimal soft-tissue contrast. While deep learning-based synthetic CT (sCT) generation from MRI offers a promising solution, existing studies predominantly utilize small sample sizes (typically fewer than 100 cases), which may limit prediction accuracy. This study aims to investigate the impact of a large-sample training dataset on sCT generation accuracy and evaluate its dosimetric performance in frameless GKRS. Methods and Materials: A total of 246 patients treated with GKRS for meningiomas were retrospectively enrolled. Eighteen cases were randomly selected for testing, while the remaining 228 cases were partitioned into a small-sample group (28 cases, M28) and a large-sample group (200 cases, M200) to train a U-Net-based MRI-to-CT translation model. The image synthesis accuracy was evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) across the whole body, soft tissue, bone, and intra-scalp regions. For the M200 model, dosimetric verification was performed by transferring the sCT and corresponding contours into the treatment planning system. Dose-volume histogram (DVH) parameters for the gross tumor volume (GTV) and various organs at risk (OARs) were calculated and statistically compared with the ground-truth CT plans. Results The M200 model consistently outperformed the M28 model across all evaluated regions and metrics. Specifically, M200 yielded significantly lower MAE (e.g., bone: 126.55 vs. 175.95; body: 18.53 vs. 25.13) and higher SSIM (e.g., bone: 0.91 vs. 0.84) compared to M28. Visual assessment and difference maps confirmed high anatomical fidelity with minimal HU errors, primarily localized at complex bony boundaries. Dosimetric evaluation demonstrated no statistically significant differences in target coverage (D98, D95, D2) or OAR sparing between the original CT and sCT plans (all p > 0.05). The DVH curves for both the GTV and OARs were nearly perfectly superimposed. Conclusions Increasing the training sample size substantially improves the accuracy of MRI-based sCT generation, particularly in bony structures. The sCT generated by the large-sample model provides sufficient HU accuracy and dosimetric reliability for GKRS, offering a viable alternative for MRI-only treatment planning workflows.

items.abstract: Abstract Purpose Cranial MRI reaches the reading room in whatever contrast combination the scanner, site and protocol produced, and lesion appearance changes with contrast. A department that wants segmentation support must maintain a separate model for each contrast combination, a library that is hard to sustain in routine practice. We evaluated a single deep learning framework that replaces that library with contrast-specialised routing. Materials and methods The framework (OMNIA) keeps one specialist subnetwork for each MR contrast and fuses their predictions at every resolution level through a hierarchical gating network that assigns voxelwise weights. Progressive training protects each specialist's contrast-specific behaviour, and a soft allocation module routes incomplete contrast sets to the specialist channels under an availability prior. The study was retrospective, across nine collections totalling 6,336 annotated volumes, five contrasts and six pathology groups, with a healthy reference collection; six public collections were used for training and internal testing, and three institutional collections were held back for external testing. Results On the seen collections the framework reached a mean Dice of 0.8204, above every universal baseline (0.8007–0.8084) and close to dedicated per-combination pipelines (0.8250), as a single deployable model. On the unseen collections it reached 0.7951, the strongest result among single models. On multi-contrast BraTS 2021 input it scored 0.8334 against 0.8366 for fifteen dedicated models, at about one third of their storage (1.65 GB versus about 4.95 GB). Conclusion Contrast-specialised routing allows one deployable model to approach the accuracy of dedicated per-combination pipelines, on data and contrast combinations beyond those it was trained on.

items.abstract: Abstract Background : Axillary lymph node (ALN) status is a critical determinant of breast cancer staging and treatment planning. This study aimed to develop and validate a habitat-based multimodal deep learning (HMDL) model that learns whole-tumor and habitat subregion-level multiparametric MRI features, radiomics features, and clinical features within a unified network to enable noninvasive preoperative prediction of ALN metastasis in breast cancer. Methods : This retrospective study enrolled 201 patients with breast cancer from two centers. At Center 1, 160 patients were randomly divided into training (n = 128) and internal validation (n = 32) sets at the patient level in an 8:2 ratio. The remaining 41 patients from Center 2 served as an independent external validation set. A two-stage 3D U-Net was used for automatic segmentation of the breast tumor region of interest (ROI). Based on dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE), fat-suppressed T2-weighted imaging (T2FS), and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), K-means clustering was applied to partition intratumoral voxels into habitat subregions, and radiomics features were extracted from the whole tumor and each subregion. The HMDL model used a 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) as the backbone, extracting whole-tumor and habitat subregion image features along three orthogonal planes, fusing them via cross-modal and cross-region multi-head self-attention into a unified imaging representation, and concatenating it with radiomics and clinical features for classification. Ablation experiments were performed to evaluate the contribution of each information source, input sequence, and input strategy. Clinical and clinical-habitat radiomics models were constructed as comparators, and DeLong tests were used to compare the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) among the three models. Results : The automatic segmentation model achieved Dice similarity coefficients of 0.842 and 0.804 on the internal and external validation sets, respectively. Based on the Calinski-Harabasz index, each tumor was partitioned into 3 habitat subregions. Ablation experiments showed that removing habitat subregion representations, radiomics features, clinical features, or any single sequence decreased the AUC on both validation sets. Among the three sequences, removal of DWI caused the largest AUC decrease in the HMDL (w/o DWI) model (AUC, 0.702 and 0.676, respectively), with statistically significant differences (P = 0.015, P = 0.012). The HMDL model achieved AUCs of 0.929 and 0.913 on the internal and external validation sets, respectively, both higher than the clinical-habitat radiomics model (0.869 and 0.841) and the clinical model (0.736 and 0.709). The difference between the HMDL and clinical models was statistically significant on the external validation set (P = 0.027). Conclusions : The HMDL model enables noninvasive quantitative prediction of ALN metastasis in breast cancer by jointly optimizing whole-tumor and habitat subregion-level imaging information, radiomics features, and clinical features within a unified network end-to-end, and demonstrates robust performance in independent external validation, offering a novel technical approach for preoperative ALN assessment.

items.abstract: Rationale and objectives Our study aimed to develop a delta deep learning radiomics model for predicting World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology (WHO/ISUP) grade in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) and to find relevant biomarkers and explore the potential biological mechanisms. Material and methods This multicenter cohort of 754 patients with ccRCC from five hospitals was split into training and internal validation cohorts in a 7:3 ratio, along with an external validation cohort (n=221) from three other hospitals. Radiomics and deep learning features were extracted from the tumor regions on multiphase contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT). Delta features were calculated as the absolute differences between features from different imaging phases. The selected features were used to develop delta deep learning radiomics signatures using different classifiers. The diagnostic performance in each model was assessed. Furthermore, gene expression profiling was conducted to for exploratory analysis of biological correlates associated with the model's grade predictions. Results The delta model achieved AUCs of 0.736 (95% CI 0.671-0.801) and 0.701 (95% CI 0.635-0.768) in the internal and external validation cohorts, respectively, which were numerically higher than those of the original model based on traditional deep learning radiomics features and demographic baseline clinical model. Additionally, the delta model demonstrated good calibration and a higher net benefit. Bioinformatics and multiomics analysis revealed that high-grade risk-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were associated with inflammation-related pathways, providing preliminary exploratory biological insights into the model's predictions. Conclusion The delta model demonstrated promising performance in WHO/ISUP grade. DEGs in predicted high-grade ccRCC were associated with inflammation-related pathways.

items.abstract: Rice blast caused by Magnaporthe oryzae threatens rice production, and genomic prediction may accelerate identification of resistant germplasm. We evaluated classical machine-learning and simulated quantum-kernel models for binary and three-class prediction of leaf blast (BL) and panicle blast (PB) resistance in 204 rice accessions with 2,120 repeated phenotypic observations. Models used 328,597 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), 104,068 phased haplotypes, or 49,451 unphased haplotypes. Binary prediction outperformed three-class prediction. The highest binary macro-F1 scores were 0.87 for BL and 0.73 for PB. Phased and unphased haplotypes reduced predictor dimensionality by 68.3% and 85.0%, respectively, while retaining broadly comparable performance. Quantum support vector classification achieved competitive results in selected binary tasks but did not consistently exceed the strongest classical models. These findings establish a benchmark for SNP- and haplotype-based prediction of rice blast resistance and for evaluation of quantum machine learning in crop genomics.

items.abstract: Computational methods are a growing component of every scientific discipline, but the pace of training and expertise for using these methods has not kept up with their widening usage. Researchers expect state-of-the-art methods to be able to independently explore their results, and do so dynamically and interactively. Producing such an application which implements a new algorithm, even though it would access a much wider audience, is typically beyond the expertise and time constraints of computational method developers. Here, we show our Sparrowhawk framework can rapidly create an interactive web application to run interactive analysis on a user's machine, across a wide range of algorithms. Focusing first on genomic epidemiology, a domain with a specific need for such methods, we created novel lightweight methods for genome assembly, antimicrobial resistance gene annotation, and taxonomic identification. Our results exceed performance of previous lightweight methods, and produce results that reproduce or closely match previous analysis pipelines. By using WebAssembly, our framework benefits from not requiring installation, command line knowledge, or transferring sensitive data over an internet connection. We show how algorithms from other researchers, and spanning fields from machine learning to physics, can rapidly be ported to web tools using our framework. We demonstrate an immediate impact on microbial bioinformatics, but expect that uptake of Sparrowhawk by developers of other tools broadly will help other researchers, and create new tools for teaching and public engagement. Thanks to the broad availability and familiarity with web browser tools across society, Sparrowhawk has the potential to significantly lower the barrier to entry to advanced computational methods.

items.abstract: Abstract Background MN is a prevalent primary glomerular disease causing adult nephrotic syndrome. Clinically, invasive renal biopsy acts as the pathological gold standard, while the widely used serological anti-PLA2R antibody has limited sensitivity and cannot reflect glomerular lesion severity. Conventional immunosuppressive regimens face frequent drug resistance and relapse, and core tissue-derived pathogenic regulators remain poorly defined. This study aimed to to identify reliable MN biomarkers and clarify underlying mechanisms,providing new approaches for precise diagnosis and treatment Methods Glomeruli from 5 MN patients and 8 normal controls were isolated via LCM and detected by LC-MRM-MS proteomics. We integrated GO/KEGG enrichment, PPI network, WGCNA, three machine learning algorithms to screen hub proteins. IHC and WB were used to verify candidate protein expression. Public single-cell dataset GSE241302 was applied for in silico knockdown simulation, and AutoDock Vina performed molecular docking to screen targeted small-molecule compounds. Results We identified 29 glomerular DEPs (18 upregulated, 11 downregulated) enriched in complement-coagulation, lipid metabolism, oxidative stress and ECM remodeling. PPI and WGCNA revealed APOE, FBLN1 and HP as core hub proteins. Three machine learning algorithms converged on HPT, FBLN1 and APOE as diagnostic markers with AUC>0.95. IHC and WB confirmed markedly higher glomerular APOE in MN (p = 0.0035, p < 0.0001). In silico APOE knockdown restored glutathione metabolism, detoxification, lipid signaling and tubular SLC transporters to relieve podocyte damage and proteinuria. Eight high-affinity APOE-targeted BRD compounds were screened via molecular docking, with BRD-K76617868 and BRD-K93023739 showing the best binding capacity. Conclusion APOE acts as a high-performance glomerular diagnostic biomarker and central pathogenic hub of MN, which mediates renal damage via crosstalk of lipid metabolism, immune inflammation, redox imbalance and tubular dysfunction. This research provides novel theoretical basis for non-invasive auxiliary diagnosis and molecular targeted therapy of MN

items.abstract: Abstract Background Insomnia is consistently associated with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) in observational studies, but the causal relationship and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the causal relationship between insomnia and late-onset AD and to identify molecular pathways and candidate genes that may contribute to this association by integrating genetic causal inference with transcriptomics. Methods Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) was performed using 28 single-nucleotide polymorphisms as instruments, with insomnia genome-wide association study summary statistics from UK Biobank (336,965 participants of European ancestry) and late-onset AD data from FinnGen (11,359 cases and 508,613 controls). Inverse-variance weighting was the primary method. Robustness was assessed using MR-Egger, weighted median, simple mode, and weighted mode estimates, together with pleiotropy, heterogeneity, and leave-one-out analyses. GEO datasets GSE122063 and GSE110226 were integrated for differential expression, weighted gene co-expression network, protein interaction, and functional enrichment analyses. Lasso regression and support vector machine recursive feature elimination were used to identify key candidate genes, whose discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves. Results Inverse-variance weighting associated genetically predicted insomnia with higher odds of late-onset AD (OR = 3.36, 95% CI 1.02–10.99; P = 0.045). Other MR methods yielded directionally consistent but imprecise estimates. The MR-Egger intercept test found no evidence of directional pleiotropy (P = 0.939), and Cochran’s Q test was not statistically significant (P = 0.062). No individual instrument dominated the leave-one-out results. Transcriptomic analysis identified 1,616 differentially expressed genes and eight co-expression modules. MEpink, MEblack, and MEbrown showed the strongest associations with AD. Their intersection with 2,330 insomnia-related genes yielded 35 candidates, enriched mainly in neuroinflammation, cell adhesion, and lipid metabolism. Both machine learning algorithms selected seven key candidates. All seven were differentially expressed between AD and controls in the combined dataset, with individual AUCs above 0.75. Conclusion Genetic liability to insomnia may be associated with an increased risk of late-onset AD. Neuroinflammation and lipid metabolism may link the two conditions, and seven candidate genes warrant further study. Given the borderline MR result, wide confidence interval, tissue heterogeneity, and absence of independent external validation, these findings require confirmation in larger multi-ancestry cohorts, independent transcriptomic datasets, and experimental studies.

items.abstract: Bile acids (BAs) are essential signaling molecules whose enterohepatic circulation (EHC) is disrupted across hepatobiliary disorders. Despite their potential as biomarkers, clinical utility is limited by high inter-individual variability, the inability of accessible peripheral blood to reflect true hepatic exposure, and the difficulty of directly measuring key physiological parameters governing the EHC. While mechanistic models can infer inaccessible hepatic profiles and patient-specific parameters from peripheral blood, personalizing them is computationally prohibitive due to multiscale dynamics causing numerical stiffness and the thousands of evaluations required for Bayesian inference. To overcome this, we developed an accelerated Bayesian inference pipeline combining timescale model reduction with neural network surrogates. Eigenvector participation factor analysis of a human EHC model revealed that rapid portal vein and hepatic sinusoidal transport drive stiffness. Applying the quasi-steady state approximation to these fast variables reduced integration times by over 97% with an integrated relative error <1.0%. A neural network surrogate further accelerated population ensemble Markov chain Monte Carlo inference from days to hours, accurately recovering parameter distributions in 100 virtual individuals 95-98% coverage. Crucially, this tractability allowed us to dissect EHC physiological mechanisms and their disease perturbation. Single fasting measurements yielded practical non-identifiability due to strong posterior correlations among hepatic synthesis, intestinal motility, and absorption. A systematic comparison of sampling protocols showed peripheral sampling at multiple time points progressively disentangles these processes, while portal vein sampling offers no added benefit. Three peripheral time points emerged as an optimal protocol, recovering >90% of the identifiability of five time points. Furthermore, the framework captured EHC compensatory dynamics, revealing a persistent positive correlation between intestinal transit and absorption. By making stiff EHC models tractable, our framework guides clinical study design and enables minimally invasive, mechanistic characterization of BA dysregulation, advancing our mechanistic understanding and personalized diagnosis of hepatobiliary diseases.

items.abstract: Staining and scanning variation impairs pathology foundation model (FM) generalization. We propose DELTA, a training-free, label-free method for post-hoc correction of FM embeddings. DELTA estimates recurrent directions from paired embedding differences between original patches and counterfactual stain-appearance variants preserving spatial structure, then attenuates aligned components through a fixed projection. Estimation from 4% of eligible patches per source dataset required no separately acquired matched images. Operators directly correct stored embeddings. On PathoROB, DELTA improved patch-level representation robustness over raw embeddings in all 20 FMs. Mean classification gains over established correction methods persisted after patch aggregation. DELTA provided additional gains after stain normalization. Whole-slide analyses showed improved in-distribution survival discrimination in TCGA-BRCA and normative cancer screening in a clinical cohort. Operators from TCGA-BRCA reduced embedding variation in the PLISM dataset across 13 staining conditions and 7 scanners without refitting. With projection rank and center matched, DELTA outperformed projections from mismatched pairs in retrieval and tissue-category concordance. items.abstract: Abstract Early detection of eye diseases is critical to the prevention of vision loss and timely clinical intervention to improve clinical outcomes. In this study, we are proposing a new deep learning framework for multi-class retinal image classification that is based on the ConvNeXt-Tiny architecture. The proposed approach was evaluated using two publicly available datasets namely, ODIR-5K (8 classes) and Eye Disease (4 classes). We trained and compared two model configurations. First, a baseline ConvNeXt-Tiny and its' enhanced variant which was the augmented with Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention blocks. The baseline model achieved 92% accuracy on ODIR-5K and 91% on Eye Disease datasets which are equal or better than present published results. With the addition of SE attention resulted in improved performance with 96% accuracy on ODIR-5K and 95% on Eye Disease. F1 scores and recall also improved with difficult classes such as Normal and Glaucoma. These results demonstrate that by integrating channel-wise attention into a lightweight CNN–Transformer hybrid backbone improves feature discrimination and generalization across datasets. Our approach offers a robust and computationally efficient solution for creating automated retinal disease screening.

items.abstract: Abstract Background In 2022 we derived and validated the ABCDMed score to predict extubation failure. Machine learning models (MLM) for the same outcome now report areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of up to 0.98. We asked whether flexible algorithms, given the same patients may improve on a model built from clinical judgement. Methods. A secondary analysis of a original prospective cohort of 800 consecutive adults extubated on a ICU in Bogotá, Colombia, at 2,600 m above sea level was performed. Extubation failure prediction was compared with two MLM, random forest, gradient boosting, and with nine further strategies, under 10 times repeated stratified 5-fold cross validation in which imputation, scaling, resampling, variable selection and hyperparameter search were performed inside training folds only, and every arm received the same candidate variables. Artificial intelligence was used in two further roles: to appraise 14 published machine learning studies of this outcome against the same reporting items, and to produce an adversarial peer review of this manuscript, every claim of which was verified by re-analysis. Results. Extubation failure occurred in 71 patients (8.9%). The published points score reproduced exactly, separating four risk strata with observed failure rates of 4.4%, 7.7%, 11.6% and 23.0%, but the score distributions of patients who failed and succeeded overlap almost completely. Given the same 12 candidate variables, random forest reached 0.630 and gradient boosting 0.627 against 0.655 for ordinary logistic regression, a spread of 0.028 in a design that cannot detect less than 0.068. Given all 42 variables, tuning, assembling and class rebalancing, no strategy exceeded the original score; SMOTE oversampling left discrimination unchanged while inflating predicted risk by 75% and driving net benefit below the treat-no strategy. Among the 14 published studies, 12 displayed an explainability figure, 7 reported calibration, 4 had any external validation, 3 reported net benefit, 3 shared code and none used repeated or nested cross validation. Conclusions. Artificial intelligence excels at extracting patterns from existing datasets, but it cannot generate information that is not there. In this cohort, neither advanced MLM nor extensive algorithmic tuning outperformed a parsimonious model based on clinical judgment.

items.abstract: Abstract Background Voice-based artificial intelligence may offer a noninvasive approach to identifying patients at elevated risk for laryngeal cancer, but successful implementation depends on its acceptability and fit within primary care. This study examined primary care clinicians’ approaches to persistent dysphonia, perceptions of artificial intelligence–assisted voice-based risk stratification, and factors influencing clinical implementation. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional mixed-methods study using semi-structured interviews and an anonymous electronic survey that could be completed independently. Interviews explored dysphonia evaluation, referral practices, technology use, and perceived implementation considerations. Survey items assessed clinical reasoning using two dysphonia vignettes, technology readiness, application acceptability, and perceived barriers. Survey responses were summarized using descriptive statistics; no inferential statistical testing was performed. Interviews were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis, and qualitative and quantitative findings were subsequently integrated at the aggregate level. Results Fifteen clinicians participated in interviews, and 16 anonymous survey responses were received. In a clinical vignette of a patient with a smoking history who presented for persistent dysphonia, all respondents identified laryngeal or other head and neck malignancy in the differential diagnosis, compared with 12 of 15 (80.0%) for a similar clinical vignette without a smoking history. Thirteen of 16 survey respondents (81.3%) reported a positive or very positive initial impression of the proposed application, and 11 (68.8%) were comfortable or very comfortable integrating it into clinical practice. Interviews revealed that clinicians generally lacked a standardized pathway for escalating persistent dysphonia and viewed artificial intelligence primarily as decision support rather than a replacement for clinical judgment. Acceptance was conditional on demonstrated accuracy, minimal workflow disruption, appropriate clinician oversight, efficient referral pathways, and attention to equity, privacy, and accountability. Conclusions Primary care clinicians demonstrated interest in voice-based artificial intelligence for laryngeal cancer risk stratification, but willingness to adopt the technology depended on more than diagnostic performance. Successful implementation will require integration into existing workflows, preservation of clinical oversight, clear pathways from risk identification to definitive evaluation, and attention to patient trust and equitable access.

items.abstract: Abstract Background and purpose Accurate applicator reconstruction is essential for dose calculation in CT-based brachytherapy. Reconstruction errors—driven by limited CT slice thickness and metal artifacts—can produce clinically relevant dose deviations. We developed a fully automated quality assurance (QA) pipeline that combines deep learning classification and segmentation with high-resolution template registration to verify the geometric accuracy of planned source dwell positions. Materials and methods We retrospectively collected 3,702 treatment plans from 742 gynecological cancer patients. A lightweight 3D convolutional neural network classified applicators into five categories, and an nnU-Net (v2) model segmented the three channels of Fletcher applicators. High-resolution (0.6-mm) template centerlines were registered to 3-mm clinical CT images using a progressive weighted arc-segment Kabsch algorithm. Geometric consistency was quantified with point-to-curve Euclidean distances. Error-detection performance was assessed in a simulation study in which one randomly selected dwell position per plan was displaced by 1, 3, or 5 mm (50 plans per magnitude), with 50 error-free plans as controls. Results The classification model achieved 99.28% accuracy and a weighted F1 score of 0.99. The segmentation model yielded a mean Dice coefficient of 90.7% and a 95% Hausdorff distance of approximately 1 mm. Mean distances between auto-segmented centerlines and the registered template curve ranged from 0.39 to 0.70 mm; mean dwell-point-to-template distances were 0.34–0.51 mm. In the simulation study, specificity was 94.0%; sensitivity was 36.0% for 1-mm displacements and 100% for both 3-mm and 5-mm displacements. Conclusion The proposed pipeline enables automated, high-precision QA of brachytherapy dwell positions and reliably detects displacements of 3 mm or larger, providing an objective tool for clinical treatment-plan verification that mitigates thick-slice artifacts through high-resolution template registration.

items.abstract: Abstract Background This study aimed to construct a pretreatment contrast-enhanced CT (CECT)-based multimodal model for noninvasive forecasting of early treatment response in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients with portal vein tumor thrombosis (PVTT) who received hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy combined with tyrosine kinase inhibitors and PD-1 inhibitors (HTI). Methods We retrospectively enrolled 116 patients with HCC and PVTT receiving HTIs (2019–2024), randomly divided 7:3 into training (n = 81) and test (n = 35) cohorts. Early objective response was assessed 6–8 weeks after treatment using modified RECIST. Radiomic features were extracted from three-dimensional volumes of interest of the primary tumor and PVTT; deep features from the largest axial tumor slice using ResNet101. Six models were developed; the final radiomic–deep learning–clinical (RCLD) model integrated out-of-fold component probabilities. Discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and overall survival (OS) stratification were evaluated. Results Sixty-eight patients responded (complete response, n = 3; partial response, n = 65); the objective response rate was 58.6% and disease control rate 91.4%. Four radiomic and three deep learning features were selected; cirrhosis was the only clinical variable. RCLD achieved the highest AUC (training 0.965, 95% CI 0.929–1.000; test 0.924, 95% CI 0.822–1.000). In the test cohort, RCLD outperformed clinical-only and radiomics–clinical models ( p = 0.003 and p = 0.026), with no significant differences from other imaging-based models. RCLD stratified OS (training P = 0.003; test P = 0.027). Conclusion A pretreatment CECT-based multimodal model integrating radiomics, deep learning, and cirrhosis predicted early objective response and stratified OS risk in HCC with PVTT receiving HTIs. Prospective multicenter validation is required.

items.abstract: Abstract To noninvasively assess the chronicity of chronic kidney disease (CKD) using a machine learning (ML) model based on superb microvascular imaging (SMI) ultrasound radiomics, and to develop and validate a clinical-radiomics nomogram for individualized prediction. A total of 305 patients with CKD confirmed by renal biopsy were prospectively enrolled and divided into training (n = 213) and test (n = 92) cohorts. Radiomic features were extracted from SMI ultrasound images of the renal cortex. The most valuable features were selected using univariate analysis, Spearman correlation analysis, and the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) algorithm. Five ML algorithms—logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbor, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost)—were trained and compared. A clinical-radiomics nomogram was constructed by integrating the radiomics score (Rad-score) with independent clinical predictors. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). The XGBoost model demonstrated the best diagnostic performance among the five ML algorithms, with areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) of 0.903 and 0.888 in the training and test cohorts, respectively. Sex and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were identified as independent clinical predictors. The combined clinical-radiomics nomogram, integrating the Rad-score with these clinical factors, showed excellent discrimination, with AUCs of 0.949 and 0.943 in the training and test cohorts, respectively. Calibration curves demonstrated good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities, and DCA confirmed the clinical utility of the nomogram. The ML classifier based on SMI ultrasound radiomics provides a promising noninvasive approach for assessing CKD chronicity. The nomogram combining SMI radiomic features with clinical characteristics offers clinicians comprehensive and personalized imaging information, which may facilitate individualized treatment decision-making.

items.abstract: Abstract Background and Aim: Maternal mortality and childbirth complications remain significant challenges in many developing countries, particularly in rural areas. Early identification of childbirth risks is crucial for reducing mortality rates. This study employs a range of machine learning techniques to identify key features related to Birth Mode and determine the most effective predictive model. The analysis is primarily based on data from the BDHS 2017–2018, aiming to improve risk prediction and ultimately enhance maternal health outcomes. Methods To identify key factors influencing birth mode, the Boruta algorithm was applied. The optimal predictive framework was then determined by evaluating several machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest (RF), Bagging, GradientBoost (GB), XGBoost (eXtreme Gradient Boosting), and AdaBoost (Adaptive Boosting). The best model was selected based on performance metrics such as precision, sensitivity, specificity, F-score, accuracy, and AUC value. Results The chi-square test revealed a significant association between birth mode and factors such as division, place of residence, age at first birth, number of living children, husband's education, respondent's employment status, wealth index, iron intake during pregnancy, education level, and BMI, all at a 1% significance level. The Boruta algorithm identified 13 key features, including those from the chi-square test, plus two additional ones. Ensemble models (RF, Bagging, GB, XGBoost, AdaBoost) were trained using these features. Bagging exhibited the highest accuracy (0.7611), precision (0.7746), F-score (0.8278), and sensitivity (0.8887). XGBoost achieved the highest specificity (0.8962), while AdaBoost had the best AUC (0.7833). Overall, Bagging outperformed the other models across four out of six metrics. Conclusions The study demonstrates the effectiveness of the Bagging algorithm for predicting birth mode, providing important insights into the factors associated with caesarean deliveries. The findings indicate a higher likelihood of caesarean sections among women from wealthier socioeconomic groups compared to those from lower-income backgrounds. This observation underscores the importance of increasing awareness regarding the potential risks and overuse of caesarean procedures, particularly among higher-income populations. The results suggest that incorporating these identified risk factors into clinical decision-making and public health strategies may support healthcare providers and policymakers in Bangladesh in reducing the prevalence of unnecessary caesarean deliveries.

items.abstract: Abstract Smartphone imaging and lightweight machine-learning readouts are extending colloidal gold-based lateral flow immunoassays (LFIAs) from subjective visual tests toward objective and multiplexed point-of-care screening. In this study, a dual-line LFIA integrated with lightweight machine learning was developed to simultaneously determine alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), in which two spatially separated test lines generated parallel signals. LFIA images were acquired using a smartphone. Regions corresponding to the control line, two test lines, and their adjacent backgrounds were identified using predefined geometric constraints. Mean RGB values were converted into RGB vector magnitudes, and background-corrected test-line features were obtained by subtracting the corresponding local background signals. The resulting one-dimensional features were analyzed using two lightweight machine-learning algorithms: k-nearest neighbors (KNN) for concentration-interval classification and Gaussian process regression (GPR) for quantitative prediction. Under the optimal conditions, the limits of detection were 4.61 ng mL⁻¹ for AFP and 5.46 ng mL⁻¹ for CEA in human serum. The overall classification accuracy reached 0.91 for both biomarkers. In 32 clinical serum samples, the ROC AUCs were 0.973 for AFP and 0.914 for CEA, increasing to 0.992 when both biomarkers were combined. The dual-line LFIA combined lightweight machine-learning workflow improves the objectivity and analytical utility of the conventional colorimetric LFIAs.

items.abstract: Abstract Objective To test whether a publicly released ECG foundation model respects the International Recommendations for ECG interpretation in athletes, and whether its errors can be corrected without athlete data. Methods We applied ECGFounder, trained on about 10 million hospital ECGs, to non-athletes with only training-related (“green”) findings (PTB-XL, Chapman/Ningbo) and to two athlete groups: 26 Norwegian endurance athletes read as normal by a cardiologist and 156 green-only recordings from 52 Spanish footballers. In a sequence of pre-registered steps we tested four fixes, anchoring sensitivity on screening-relevant abnormal ECGs, and confirmed the best fix with thresholds set on data it had never seen. Results Green-only ECGs were called abnormal in 33.7% of PTB-XL and 17.9% of Chapman/Ningbo cases, and the model called abnormal 34.6% of normal endurance athletes and 47.4% of footballer recordings, sometimes labelling infarction. Rules applied over the model’s own named findings, with or without measured intervals, made things worse. A small readout retrained on the model’s features with athlete-criteria labels, using non-athletes only, called 17.6% (95% CI 10.3% to 25.4%) of normal athletes abnormal against 52.8% for the model’s own output, at 87.5% against 89.4% sensitivity for screening-relevant abnormal ECGs, and held across three training seeds. Conclusion The model’s representation already separates athletic adaptation from disease; its default output does not. Relabelling the readout against the International Criteria removes about two-thirds of the false alarms.

items.abstract: Abstract Patient-derived xenografts (PDXs) are critical models for translational oncology, but their computational use is limited by fragmented pharmacogenomic data, inconsistent response annotations, and poor access to raw longitudinal tumour-volume measurements. Here we present XevaDB (xevadb.ca), a standardized platform designed to support machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) applications through the integration of longitudinal treatment and control-arm tumour growth curves with harmonized drug and gene annotations, response metrics, replicate-level experimental design, clinical annotation, and matched molecular profiles. XevaDB provides access to data from 689 PDX models across six tumour types, 69 drugs, 4,828 treatment-control experiments, and matched RNA-seq, copy-number, and mutation data for 337 models. Through four case studies, we show that preserving raw longitudinal response data enables analyses beyond conventional static endpoints: transcriptomic prediction of intrinsic tumour growth, image-based deep learning of drug-response trajectories, replicate-aware transfer learning from cell-line-trained models, and multi-omics prediction of paclitaxel response. These results establish XevaDB as a resource for sharing standardized longitudinal pharmacogenomic data and enabling reproducible AI/ML modeling, demonstrating how integrated PDX data can accelerate computational approaches in preclinical cancer research.

items.abstract: Abstract Recent methods enable incorporation of experimental data, such as chemical crosslinks, X-ray and cryo-EM density maps, into AlphaFold to guide the predictions towards structures consistent with the input data. However, it is unclear how these methods balance the input data with AlphaFold’s learned structural priors. To probe this aspect, we curated a benchmark of homomeric and heteromeric protein complexes non-redundant with the AlphaFold training set. We evaluated three methods, AlphaLink2, Boltz2, and GRASP, on the benchmark, using chemical crosslinks as input data. All methods predict structures that satisfy the crosslinks well, in the easy case, where 90% of the input crosslinks are consistent with a single structure. Yet this apparent success belies important limitations. First, for most complexes, the methods produce nearly identical predictions with and without the input crosslinks. Second, predictions remain largely unchanged from the easy case even as the fraction of false-positive crosslinks increases, even though satisfying these crosslinks would require sampling conformations that differ substantially from those predicted in the easy case. Finally, when challenged with input crosslinks from multiple states, the methods remain biased toward a single state. Together, these findings suggest that current AlphaFold-based approaches can be insufficiently sensitive to the input data, with the predictions likely driven primarily by the learned structural priors. Our study underscores the need for AF-based IM approaches that can weigh experimental evidence better and can capture structural heterogeneity. The benchmark and all code to obtain the predictions and perform the analysis are available at https://github.com/isblab/af_im.

items.abstract: Proline metabolism is implicated in tumor development and plays a crucial role in redox balance in plants. The P5CS enzyme is responsible for initiating proline biosynthesis from glutamate. P5CS has two catalytic domains and originated from a fusion event between the γ-GK and γ-GPR enzymes. Plants, animals, and some unicellular eukaryotes possess the P5CS gene, whereas prokaryotes, fungi, and some algae encode the non-fused enzymes, γ-GK and γ-GPR. Previous evolutionary studies suggested that all P5CS genes are derived from a single fusion event. They also reported some possible cases of reversion to one-domain forms, like in Trypanosomatida. Here, we address the evolutionary relationship among P5CS, γ-GK, and γ-GPR enzymes by analyzing their three-dimensional structures and reviewing their functional aspects. Using models from 15 proteins from nine species, available in the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database, which we classified into the following groups: plant and animal P5CS, γ-GK and γ-GPR, trypanosomatid P5CS, complete, and reversion case. Our structural comparisons reinforce the fold similarity among them and highlight significant differences between P5CS and the non-fused γ-GK and γ-GPR. Among them, the bona fide γ-GPR enzymes have an extra loop portion, absent in the fused form, P5CS. This loop is lacking in the trypanosomatid 'γ-GPR', which probably indicates a lineage of P5CS that has lost the GK domain, reinforcing the reversion hypothesis. Here, for the first time, we suggest the catalytic mechanism of the GPR domain and detail the conserved residues involved in ATP binding in the GK domain.

items.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) control eukaryotic cell-cycle progression by phosphorylating specific substrates with substrate recognition often involving cyclin-specific docking interactions. However, in minimal cell cycle control systems driven by a single cyclin-CDK complex, how docking interactions contribute to the differential timing of substrate phosphorylation remains unclear. Here, we used AlphaFold-Multimer to systematically predict interactions between the fission yeast mitotic cyclin-CDK fusion Cdc13-L-Cdc2 and its known in vivo CDK substrates. We found that many substrates are predicted to interact with the cyclin hydrophobic patch, and have identified a previously uncharacterised docking motif, [FVIPWGLAM](x)xER[LMV] (ERL motif), with features consistent with an atypical RxL motif. We show that ERL motifs can functionally substitute for canonical RxL motifs to promote phosphorylation of a model CDK substrate by Cdc13-Cdc2, while the S-phase cyclin-CDK Cig2-Cdc2 was found to preferentially phosphorylate substrates containing canonical RxL motifs. Interestingly, Cdc13-L-Cdc2 was not predicted to bind DNA replication substrates preferentially over mitotic substrates, suggesting that other mechanisms underlie the temporal ordering of CDK substrate phosphorylation. These results reveal that cyclin-CDK-substrate interactions are more diverse than previously thought.

items.summary: Learning and inference on time series can pose significant statistical challenges, including autocorrelated observations, distribution shift over time, and the curse of dimensionality. items.abstract: Learning and inference on time series can pose significant statistical challenges, including autocorrelated observations, distribution shift over time, and the curse of dimensionality. These challenges complicate the practical application of causal discovery algorithms, which already suffer from high computational and sample complexity in the general case. To mitigate these issues, this work introduces Iterative Temporal Parent Discovery (ITPD): a sound and complete constraint-based procedure for causal structure learning on multivariate time series with causal nonstationarity. ITPD takes a local-to-global learning approach that discovers the global graph by sequentially discovering the parent set for each variable. ITPD exploits temporal structural priors, graph partitioning, and the local Markov condition to swap higher-order conditional independence tests for lower-order alternatives. With an exact oracle, ITPD performed the least number of tests and used the smallest average conditioning set sizes relative to baselines. In benchmarking simulations, ITPD sat on the Pareto frontier with respect to F1 and wall-clock time and was faster than baselines on large graphs (geq 1000 nodes). For graphs with 2000 nodes, ITPD ran 2.3times, 9.1times, and 40.9times faster than iterative IAMB, DF-PC, and PCMCI, respectively.

items.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable robots to perform diverse tasks from visual observations and language instructions. While prior work has explored task suppression and refusal, stopping prohibited behavior once execution is underway and controlling the resulting physical response remain challenging. Our evaluation reveals that policies which suppress a task from its initial state can still complete it when taking over partway through execution. Even when the task remains unfinished, the robot may drop a held object, making non-completion an incomplete measure of safety. To address these challenges, we introduce State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) for tasks where holding provides an appropriate alternative response. SAFI comprises two stages, (1) fallback target construction, which assigns stationary arm commands and consistent gripper targets throughout prohibited-task demonstrations, and (2) joint policy adaptation, which learns these targets alongside the original actions of retained tasks. This supervision teaches an explicit alternative response at intermediate execution states while maintaining the robot's other skills. Extensive experiments with OpenVLA-OFT across LIBERO and BadLIBERO tasks evaluate prohibited completion, physical incidents, and retained-task performance. On the evaluated LIBERO tasks, SAFI reduces aggregate target success after takeover to 1.3\%, with no recorded physical incidents or action saturation, while preserving high retained-task success.

items.abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving increasingly depends on scaling training demonstrations, yet data growth does not guarantee proportional gains. However, additional data do not guarantee better policies: a demonstration that benefits one planner may be redundant or harmful to another. Existing curation methods typically infer data value from intrinsic sample properties or training-dependent proxies that do not measure downstream policy utility. To address this, we introduce Policy-Aware Data Valuation (PAD), a framework that assigns each candidate demonstration a utility specific to the target driving policy. PAD combines scene-level calibration feedback with projected policy gradients and a regularized approximation of local training geometry, producing scalable influence-based values for the policy. A controlled group-removal study establishes the directional fidelity of these values, while cross-planner analysis shows that the same candidate pool induces markedly different rankings across planner families. On DiffusionDrive, PAD improves EPDMS over real-only training by 3.5 points on NavTest and 5.0 points on NavHard. Policy-specific curation consistently outperforms real-only and full-pool training across diffusion-, regression-, and flow-matching-based planners while substantially reducing scene-level regressions. These results establish policy-aware data valuation as a basis for replacing indiscriminate data accumulation with targeted policy improvement, enabling more efficient and reliable scaling of autonomous-driving systems.
