items.abstract: Introduction Shock wave lithotripsy (SWL) remains a cornerstone of non-invasive urolithiasis treatment, yet its success is highly variable and difficult to predict using traditional linear statistical models. Traditional models often fail to account for the complex, non-linear interactions between stone characteristics and procedural variables. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of machine learning (ML) algorithms in predicting stone-free status (SFS), post-SWL renal colic, and the requirement for subsequent ureteroscopy (URS). Materials and methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on a multicentric database of 1498 patients treated with SWL over a six-year period. A total of 23 clinical features, including patient demographics, stone characteristics (size, density, and location), and surgical parameters, were utilized as inputs. We compared 15 different ML algorithms (including LightGBM, CatBoost, and Random Forest) and a multitask Artificial Neural Network against conventional logistic regression. Models were evaluated using validation accuracy, confusion matrices, cross-imbalance metrics (AUC-ROC, AUPRC), and F1-scores. "SFS" was defined as the primary endpoint, while secondary endpoints were represented by "Need for secondary URS" and occurrence of "Post-SWL colic". Results On logistic regression analysis, stone characteristics (size, density) resulted as the most important predictors of treatment failure. Treatment parameters (sessions, power) reflected procedural difficulty, and SWL success decreases with increasing stone complexity. ML models consistently outperformed traditional logistic regression across all endpoints. For the primary endpoint (SFS), LightGBM achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.79-0.86) and an AUPRC of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.84-0.91). For secondary endpoints, the Need for secondary URS was predicted with high discrimination by LightGBM (AUC-ROC = 0.92, 95% CI: 0.89-0.95; AUPRC = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.71-0.84) and CatBoost (AUC-ROC = 0.89, 95% CI: 0.85-0.92; AUPRC = 0.73, 95% CI: 0.65-0.80). For Post-SWL colic (2.7% prevalence), LightGBM achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.82-0.93) and an AUPRC of 0.42 (95% CI: 0.31-0.54), reflecting the realistic discrimination limits for rare post-procedural events. Conclusion ML models, particularly gradient boosting algorithms, demonstrate potential in predicting outcomes after SWL. While SFS remains inherently difficult to predict due to extra-procedural factors, ML provides accurate assessments of treatment failure and complications. These tools could support more personalized clinical decision-making, helping to identify patients who may benefit from primary endoscopic intervention rather than SWL.

items.abstract: Background Lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) is a critical prognostic factor guiding adjuvant therapy in early-stage cervical cancer, yet its preoperative assessment is often limited by the spatial resolution of standard MRI. This study aimed to investigate the value of a deep learning-based 3D super-resolution (SR) MRI radiomics model in predicting LVSI and to evaluate how SR reconstruction impacts image quality and radiomic feature robustness. Methods This retrospective study included 117 patients with early-stage cervical cancer (training cohort: n = 81; validation cohort: n = 36). A 3D Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (SRGAN) reconstructed T2-SPAIR and DWI sequences into super-resolution images (SRI) with a 4× upsampling factor. Radiomic features were extracted, and an SRI-based multimodal fusion model was developed and systematically compared with original image (OI)-based and clinical models using the Area Under the Curve (AUC) and Decision Curve Analysis (DCA). Results SR reconstruction significantly improved the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for both DWI (P = 0.012) and T2-SPAIR (P = 0.030). For DWI, SRI preserved intratumoral texture heterogeneity, leading to improved diagnostic performance (Validation AUC: SRI-DWI 0.864 vs. OI-DWI 0.727, P = 0.041). The final SRI-Fusion model achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (Validation AUC: 0.934), significantly outperforming the OI-Fusion model (AUC: 0.828, P = 0.044) and the clinical model (AUC: 0.626, P = 0.012). Conclusions SRGAN-based reconstruction effectively improves MRI quality and feature robustness, particularly in DWI. The SRI-based multimodal radiomics model demonstrates superior predictive performance for LVSI in early-stage cervical cancer compared to conventional imaging and clinical models.

items.summary: Real-world portfolio management requires converting noisy market observations into coordinated, simultaneous allocations across multiple assets under shared capital constraints. Advances in forecasting models and alpha discovery help identify opportunities. However, traditional pipelines often decouple signal forecasting from portfolio construction, potentially misaligning learning with allocation and execution…
items.abstract: Real-world portfolio management requires converting noisy market observations into coordinated, simultaneous allocations across multiple assets under shared capital constraints. Advances in forecasting models and alpha discovery help identify opportunities. However, traditional pipelines often decouple signal forecasting from portfolio construction, potentially misaligning learning with allocation and execution objectives. We present AllocFlow, an end-to-end flow-matching framework that directly generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories. To capture dependencies among portfolio positions, AllocFlow employs a cross-asset flow Transformer conditioned on temporal market representations to generate continuous, signed position weights across all instruments jointly. To address the sample inefficiency and instability of learning continuous allocation policies from scratch, we establish a two-stage training scheme: strategy-supervised imitation shapes a structured distribution of candidate portfolios, followed by group-relative reinforcement learning (RL) that refines joint decisions using portfolio-level financial rewards and a frozen policy reference. On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, RL refinement raises the annualized net return of the imitation policy from 27.79% to 51.38% and its Calmar ratio from 0.955 to 4.043, surpassing the teacher strategy on every metric, and AllocFlow reaches a Calmar ratio of 4.90 on six further months of unseen 2026 data without retraining.

While existing approaches employ learned compressed representations (e.g., continuous VAE latents) to render prediction tractable, they rely on complex neural encoders that often cap generation fidelity. Conversely, training-free targets like mel-spectrograms eliminate encoder overhead, yet their potential for autoregressive generation remains largely underexplored. In this work, we propose VoxMel, a tokenizer-free framework for autoregressive TTS that makes stable mel modeling tractable through a fixed, exactly invertible two-axis Haar transform. The transform first decomposes each mel spectrogram along frequency into local averages and a frequency residual, then splits the averaged component along time into Coarse-Mel and a temporal residual. A language-model backbone with a flow-matching head autoregressively generates Coarse-Mel. Non-autoregressive residual tiers then predict the temporal residual from Coarse-Mel, followed by the frequency residual conditioned on the reconstructed Frequency-Averaged Mel. Neither residual is fed back into the autoregressive history. Trained on 100K hours of Emilia, the supervised 0.6B model obtains 1.51\% WER and 0.738 speaker similarity (SIM) on test-en, and 1.29\% CER and 0.755 SIM on test-zh. GRPO improves these results to 1.15\% WER / 0.753 SIM and 1.17\% CER / 0.776 SIM, respectively. We also distill the guided flow head into two- and four-step students, requiring 2 or 4 head evaluations per coarse frame. The four-step student retains competitive SIM and nearly matches the supervised model in WER/CER.

items.abstract: Biomolecular design requires finding chemically and geometrically compatible arrangements of interacting atoms and molecules. The complexity of problems which can be tackled by deep learning design models is limited by both the molecular landscape they encompass and their ability to explore that landscape effectively. Here we introduce RFD4-Proteina, which addresses these limitations through intrinsic and extrinsic reasoning within a shared chemical and conformational latent space. The latent space encompasses standard and modified amino acids, sugars, DNA, and RNA, with force-field supervision favoring physically plausible atomic reconstructions. Within this space, intrinsic reasoning uses recurrent refinement to adaptively allocate computation, while extrinsic reasoning guides search with arbitrary constraints such as energetic or geometric criteria. Across in silico protein design benchmarks, RFD4-Proteina achieves higher design success rates at greater generation throughput than all previous methods evaluated, with further gains from conformational flexibility, recurrent refinement, and search. The same model performs equivalently to or better than state-of-the-art specialist methods for side-chain packing, sequence design, conformational sampling, and design refinement. We demonstrate the power and versatility of RFD4-Proteina experimentally by designing specific and cross-reactive binders to therapeutically relevant targets, recognizing phosphorylations, controlling glycosylation, and creating enzymes that catalyze both bond-breaking and bond-forming reactions, including a first proof-of-concept demonstration of a de novo designed enzyme for active pharmaceutical ingredient synthesis. By unifying diverse chemistry, conformational flexibility, and scalable reasoning in a single physically grounded latent space, RFD4-Proteina expands the frontier of biomolecular design.

items.summary: Heterogeneity in tumor regulatory programs, cellular composition and spatial organization complicates target prioritization for natural compounds. We developed a spatial-context heterogeneous graph neural network ranker (SC-HGNN-Rank) that combines relation-aware graph representations with ranking optimization to integrate compound-target associations, transcriptional regulation, interaction networks, and…
items.abstract: Heterogeneity in tumor regulatory programs, cellular composition and spatial organization complicates target prioritization for natural compounds. We developed a spatial-context heterogeneous graph neural network ranker (SC-HGNN-Rank) that combines relation-aware graph representations with ranking optimization to integrate compound-target associations, transcriptional regulation, interaction networks, and single-cell and spatial information. The model ranked 600 candidate axes in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD), hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) and gastric adenocarcinoma (STAD). Under matched training conditions, mean Spearman correlations with the reference ranking were 0.965, 0.967 and 0.976 for leave-one-cancer-out, compound-group holdout and target-group holdout evaluations, respectively. The composite ranking objective improved mean Spearman correlation by 0.049 over a simple objective using the same encoder, whereas removing the spatial module reduced it by 0.147. Model ranking and multilayer evidence prioritized Quercetin-CDK1/MYB-Myeloid in COAD, 4',5-dihydroxyflavone (4',5-DHF)-AR/HDAC1-T/NK in LIHC, and Eriodyctiol-HSP90AB1/HOPX-Fibroblast in STAD. Expanded spatial analyses with expression-matched gene controls assessed associations between target expression and mapped cell abundance. Cellular thermal shift and drug affinity responsive target stability assays showed increased retention of target proteins after compound treatment. In HCT116, JHH-6 and MKN45 cells, the compounds reduced viability, colony formation, migration and invasion cell counts, and increased apoptosis. Target knockdown produced similar growth-inhibitory phenotypes, whereas overexpression attenuated compound-induced effects, supporting the involvement of CDK1, AR and HSP90AB1 in the respective responses. The accompanying Explorer supports candidate searches, evidence inspection and data export. By incorporating regulatory and spatial contexts into natural-compound prioritization, this study provides a reusable approach and experimentally supported candidates for target-directed pharmacological research in digestive system cancers.

items.summary: Transformer language models are commonly scaled by making their blocks wider or stacking them deeper. In this work, we explore a complementary path: branching, the parallel composition of full Transformer blocks. items.abstract: Transformer language models are commonly scaled by making their blocks wider or stacking them deeper. In this work, we explore a complementary path: branching, the parallel composition of full Transformer blocks. We introduce the Multi-Branch Transformer (MBT), which processes the input through shared initial layers, executes independently parameterized branches of sequential blocks in parallel, and fuses their outputs before shared final layers. At comparable training compute, we study three MBT variants: Wide-Shallow preserves block width, Narrow-Deep preserves sequential depth, and Balanced interpolates between them. In controlled pretraining experiments at four mixture-of-experts scales (0.8B to 2.1B total parameters), 2-branch Wide-Shallow MBTs consistently outperform sequential Transformers under matched parameter and training-compute budgets. Balanced MBTs improve further and retain comparable quality as the number of branches increases. To improve inference efficiency at long contexts, we introduce Joint-KV, which constructs a shared KV cache from branch representations at each depth. Our final recipe combines Balanced MBTs with Joint-KV, supported by an inference engine that exploits branch grouping and shared-cache reuse. Fitted scaling curves indicate that standard Transformers require up to 1.26x as much training body compute to match our final models' validation loss. These models reduce full-model KV-cache storage by up to 34% and deliver up to 51.4% higher decoding throughput on a single H200 GPU. Ablation studies show that branching yields gains beyond changes in width and depth, enables an effective KV-sharing strategy (Joint-KV), remains robust across fusion functions, and performs best in the middle layers. These findings show that branching offers a practical path for scaling language models toward both better modeling quality and faster inference.

items.abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. We present JEPA4R, a JEPA world model that observes single-depth-camera point clouds, predicts and plans in their latent space, and acts through a policy head on its frozen latents; we call this 4D point planning. A decoder on the frozen world model shows what it imagines as 4D point clouds, with a mean point error within 1.1 cm over 200 steps. Under the policy-learning protocols of OGBench and CortexBench, JEPA4R leads pixel JEPA models on OGBench Cube-Single, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple and Scene, and ranks first on MetaWorld and Adroit Relocate with 98.4% and 88.0%, above the runner-up, R3M, at 96.0% and 65.3%. Trained only in a digital twin, JEPA4R and its policy heads run zero-shot on the real arm with both a gripper and a dexterous hand.

items.title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
items.summary: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit…
items.abstract: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts. To bridge the gap, we introduce SALA, which emphasizes establishing the semantic correspondence for latent actions. Without requiring paired data, we use the language descriptions of unpaired human and robot clips to estimate semantic similarities and supervise cross-embodiment correspondence. Specifically, we translate these similarities into soft neighborhood structures that guide human latent actions toward semantically related robot latents, while robot action reconstruction grounds the latent space in control. The resulting shared latent action space provides a unified supervision signal for training an embodied foundation model on both human and robot videos. Notably, latent action supervision enables scaling along two axes: (1) pre-training on increasing amounts of general human video consistently reduces robot action prediction error on downstream tasks, and (2) post-training on increasing amounts of task-specific human video substantially improves real-world robot task success rates.

items.title: Centered Ablation: Why Last-Layer Directional Ablation Under-Fires or Collapses, and a Closed-Form Fix
items.summary: Directional ablation removes a hidden state's component along a "behaviour direction" while a language model runs. It is the standard way to switch a behaviour such as refusal off, but it is erratic: on some models it barely fires, on others the text collapses into repetition. We show why, and fix it. At the last residual stream, ablation is exactly a logit bias: a fixed vocabulary footprint scaled by a gate, the…
items.abstract: Directional ablation removes a hidden state's component along a "behaviour direction" while a language model runs. It is the standard way to switch a behaviour such as refusal off, but it is erratic: on some models it barely fires, on others the text collapses into repetition. We show why, and fix it. At the last residual stream, ablation is exactly a logit bias: a fixed vocabulary footprint scaled by a gate, the cosine between the hidden state and the direction. The gate is measured from the origin, but last-layer states share a large common mode far from it, so a direction that overlaps the common mode fires on benign text and under-fires on its targets. Centered Ablation (CA) projects the common mode out of the direction, in closed form. Across 8 models, CA raises attack success by 29 and 46 points where the standard recipe under-fires, cuts collapse on Gemma-2-9B from 50\% to 1\%, and preserves 12 to 40 points more benign answers on high-overlap models, 39 to 46 more than the affine offset of prior work. Two numbers computed before generation predict, on models the analysis had not seen, which gain faithfulness and which gain attack success, and a collapse index marks when text degenerates. We also show that two standard safety judges score collapsed text in opposite directions, which can fabricate a 46-point effect.

items.title: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations
items.summary: A coding agent working within a software organization must establish what to build, collaborate with colleagues, and verify what it delivers. We introduce SWE-CoWork, a benchmark comprising 101 development assignments across 101 real repositories, 11 programming languages, and 12 application domains. Each assignment places an agent in a simulated engineering organization with 26 colleagues who have distinct…
items.abstract: A coding agent working within a software organization must establish what to build, collaborate with colleagues, and verify what it delivers. We introduce SWE-CoWork, a benchmark comprising 101 development assignments across 101 real repositories, 11 programming languages, and 12 application domains. Each assignment places an agent in a simulated engineering organization with 26 colleagues who have distinct responsibilities, bounded knowledge, and controlled collaboration behavior. Starting from a brief handoff, agents must recover requirements distributed across colleagues and workplace records, reconcile conflicting evidence, and implement changes evaluated by private executable tests. We evaluate eleven models and find a substantial gap between partial implementation and complete task delivery. The two leading models satisfy approximately 63% of fail-to-pass (F2P) tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments. Providing complete requirements upfront improves F2P by approximately 16 percentage points for Seed Evolving and GPT-6 Astra, yet leaves complete task success unchanged. Requirement-level trajectory analysis reveals failures throughout the delivery process: Claude-Opus-5.5 directs a mean of 93% of first questions about queried cards to their accountable owners across runs but obtains only 64% of colleague-held requirements. Deferred questions go unfollowed, implementations remain incomplete even after requirements are acquired, and 31% of requirements reported as completed fail their tests. These findings highlight sustained requirement tracking, from clarification through implementation, verification, and handoff, as a key challenge for reliable autonomous software engineering.

items.title: Reflection Anchors for Propagation-Aware Visual Retention in Long-Chain Multimodal Reasoning
items.summary: Long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning improves large vision--language models, but visual information often fades during generation, limiting long-horizon multimodal reasoning. Existing methods either re-inject vision at inference or train policies for stronger grounding, but where to intervene relies on perception heuristics rather than principled gain analysis, and how local visual influence propagates remains…
items.abstract: Long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning improves large vision--language models, but visual information often fades during generation, limiting long-horizon multimodal reasoning. Existing methods either re-inject vision at inference or train policies for stronger grounding, but where to intervene relies on perception heuristics rather than principled gain analysis, and how local visual influence propagates remains implicit. We study this problem from an information-theoretic standpoint and derive a lower bound on the downstream visual gain of a one-step intervention, which suggests two factors: local branching room (token entropy) and downstream visual propagation potential (suffix divergence from a vision-marginalized reference). Guided by this analysis, we propose reflection-anchor policy optimization (RAPO), a GRPO-based policy optimization method that selects high-entropy reflection anchors and optimizes a chain-masked finite-window KL surrogate for downstream visual dependence. Experiments on reasoning-intensive and general-domain benchmarks show that RAPO delivers substantial gains over strong baselines across multiple LVLM backbones. Mechanism analyses further indicate that reflection anchors are enriched for visually sensitive decision points and that RAPO increases contrastive visual-dependence signals along generated trajectories.

items.title: GlyphAtlas: Disentangling Stroke Detail from Layout for Scene Text Synthesis
items.summary: Scene text synthesis requires stroke-accurate characters rendered in a specified layout, as well as visual coherence with the surrounding scene. To achieve this, existing methods commonly pre-render the target text at its intended locations to form a glyph image that jointly specifies layout and glyph structure. However, this representation ties the resolution of each glyph to its target region, limiting…
items.abstract: Scene text synthesis requires stroke-accurate characters rendered in a specified layout, as well as visual coherence with the surrounding scene. To achieve this, existing methods commonly pre-render the target text at its intended locations to form a glyph image that jointly specifies layout and glyph structure. However, this representation ties the resolution of each glyph to its target region, limiting fine-grained stroke guidance for small, densely packed, or structurally complex text. To tackle this, we propose GlyphAtlas, a scene text synthesis framework that retains the glyph image as a spatial anchor and supplies fine-grained stroke references through a dedicated glyph atlas. The atlas renders and encodes each character or word in a separate cell, decoupling reference resolution from target-region size. We further introduce atlas-anchored attention, which lets each text region retrieve stroke detail only from its corresponding atlas cells to refine the coarse glyph structure provided by the glyph image. This coarse-to-fine conditioning simplifies stroke rendering while preserving explicit layout correspondence. We optimize GlyphAtlas with a mask-weighted flow matching objective and a timestep-weighted text perceptual loss for writing accuracy and background consistency. Random resolution augmentation of atlas cells supports adjustable atlas budgets at inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GlyphAtlas achieves stroke-accurate synthesis of small, dense, and structurally complex text, zero-shot transfer to languages unseen during task-specific training, and leading performance in scenes with many text regions. project page: https://fr0zencrane.github.io/project-glyphatlas/

What is actually new in these models, and is it tested? We put this question to LLM technical reports. We look at three things: what the reference code shows about how new open-weight architectures differ from earlier ones;…
items.abstract: In 2025 alone, 48 new large language model (LLM) architectures were added to the Hugging Face transformers library, and many of them arrive with a technical report that presents the model as new. What is actually new in these models, and is it tested? We put this question to LLM technical reports. We look at three things: what the reference code shows about how new open-weight architectures differ from earlier ones; what 40 randomly sampled technical reports claim as new and whether they support it with ablation studies; and what they disclose for reproducibility and transparency. In the library, 39 of the 48 architectures added in 2025 take at least two of their three core blocks from another model, most often Llama, although part of this reflects how the library writes code. In the reports, 19 of 73 architectural or training novelty claims come with a controlled with/without comparison; 4 of 40 reports state more than one training run; 8 rerun the models they compare against under one setup; and 1 discloses data mixture, token count, and compute together. We also looked for known components given new names: none of five candidate cases hid its origin, though we did not study model names. We propose seven reporting rules for LLM release reports and apply them to two reports. We do not judge model quality, and an untested claim may still be true.

items.title: Unreasonable Confidence from Simulator Misspecification: Directional Robustness on the SPEED+ Sim-to-Real Benchmark
items.summary: Vision-based navigation systems for orbit must be trained almost entirely on synthetic imagery, because real labelled images of a given spacecraft in flight rarely exist. Benchmarks like SPEED+ are built for that situation: the training set comes from a simulator, and the test sets are real images of a satellite mockup under two kinds of lighting. That simulator approximates how light reflects off mylar and…
items.abstract: Vision-based navigation systems for orbit must be trained almost entirely on synthetic imagery, because real labelled images of a given spacecraft in flight rarely exist. Benchmarks like SPEED+ are built for that situation: the training set comes from a simulator, and the test sets are real images of a satellite mockup under two kinds of lighting. That simulator approximates how light reflects off mylar and aluminium, and like every scientific simulator it is misspecified. Its error is radiometric, since it misses the specular highlights, hard shadows and sensor saturation common in real images. We probe the resulting synthetic-to-real gap, the central risk for such systems, with a deliberately simple monocular pose estimator. In a 2x2 study of backbone adaptation and photometric augmentation, trained on synthetic images and tested on both real hardware-in-the-loop domains, we find three things. (1) The model does not know it is failing: regions conformally calibrated to 90% on synthetic data cover only 9-15% of rotation errors on sunlamp and 21-38% on lightbox, so a wrong pose carries the confidence of a correct one. (2) Transfer is asymmetric: scaling data and features improved synthetic rotation error from 1.65 to 1.03 rad but moved the harshly lit sunlamp domain by only 0.05 rad, under twice its seed s.d., whereas adapting the backbone's last stage carried 63-83% of its extra synthetic gain to both real domains. (3) Once the backbone adapts, augmentation helps only in the direction it models: our photometric stack improved the diffusely lit lightbox domain from 1.17 to 0.99 rad on every seed but moved sunlamp no more than seed-to-seed variation, while with the backbone frozen it helped sunlamp more. Every post-review experiment was pre-registered, and the code, per-image predictions and pre-registration record are at https://github.com/lokindoo/spacecraft-pose-estimation.

items.summary: Driving world models usually generate videos from six pinhole cameras with separate optical centres and small overlaps, and must learn to keep these views consistent. We present PanDWM, which stitches them into one 360^circ panoramic band. Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on…
items.abstract: Driving world models usually generate videos from six pinhole cameras with separate optical centres and small overlaps, and must learn to keep these views consistent. We present PanDWM, which stitches them into one 360^circ panoramic band. Camera boundaries then fall inside one image, so keeping the views consistent means keeping the image continuous, and each pixel still records its camera ray. Conditioned on layouts, a causal student generates the band window by window in four steps; it is distilled from a causal teacher and trained on its own rollouts. A feed-forward decoder lifts each frame along these rays into 3D Gaussians, and static Gaussians from neighbouring frames complete them into 4D scenes. On nuScenes, scored in one stitched 360^circ view, PanDWM has lower FID and FVD than the multi-camera baselines at 8-46times their speed, and keeps its 50-step teacher's FID while lowering FVD by 22-25%.

items.title: Beyond Answering: Learning to Speak First and Act in Streaming Video
items.summary: Most AI assistants respond only when prompted, remaining silent even when events in the video stream offer meaningful opportunities for conversation. To move beyond purely user-driven interaction, we present AURA 2.0, a streaming video large language model that introduces three core upgrades to AURA. The key advance is Model-Initiated Conversation (MIC), which enables the model to identify topics worth discussing in…
items.abstract: Most AI assistants respond only when prompted, remaining silent even when events in the video stream offer meaningful opportunities for conversation. To move beyond purely user-driven interaction, we present AURA 2.0, a streaming video large language model that introduces three core upgrades to AURA. The key advance is Model-Initiated Conversation (MIC), which enables the model to identify topics worth discussing in the evolving visual stream and initiate conversations at appropriate moments without a user query. Stream-Aware Tool Calling (SATC) lets the model act on what it sees by invoking external tools using the current visual and conversational context and incorporating returned information into the ongoing interaction. Interactive Visual Grounding (IVG) supports visual grounding in both user inputs and model outputs. The model can identify objects marked by users on video frames and produce frame-aligned bounding boxes to link its responses to specific objects and regions. To develop these capabilities, we construct a dedicated streaming interaction dataset and adopt a three-stage training scheme to integrate the new behaviors with AURA's existing streaming interaction abilities. We further incorporate Long-Horizon Interaction Memory (LHIM) to maintain contextual continuity over extended video streams. Evaluations on public streaming benchmarks show that AURA 2.0 achieves leading performance among open-source streaming models, while targeted evaluations further validate its new interaction capabilities.

items.abstract: The transition from occupancy-driven small molecule inhibitors to event-driven proteolysis targeting chimeras (PROTACs) represents a paradigm shift in drug discovery, enabling the degradation of the undruggable targets. However, the heterobifunctional architecture of PROTACs inherently places these macrostructures within the beyond-Rule-of-5 (bRo5) chemical space, which is characterized by elevated molecular weights and complex polar surface areas. This chapter systematically analyzes the evolution of linkerology, transforming linkers from passive bridges into functional modules that affect the thermodynamics, kinetics, and metabolic stability of the ternary complex. Furthermore, we outline strategies for engineering target protein and E3 ligase ligands, focusing on refining structure-activity relationships, circumventing resistance via allosteric targeting, and optimizing pharmacokinetic profiles through strategic property space allocation. By integrating concepts such as the molecular chameleonicity, active transport pathways, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven generative design, this chapter offers a theoretical framework for resolving the oral bioavailability challenge. Finally, through case studies of clinical candidates such as vepdegestrant and bavdegalutamide, we illustrate the translation of these theoretical principles into clinical reality.

items.title: Translating Perivascular Inflammation Imaging into Precision Coronary Care: An Ex plainable Nomogram Integrating Pericoronary Adipose Tissue Attenuation Index with Anatomical and Functional CT Biomarkers for Acute Coronary Syndrome Discrimination
items.summary: Abstract Background: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and stable coronary artery disease (SCAD) present overlapping clinical phenotypes, yet mandate divergent therapeutic strategies—urgent revascularization versus pharmacological optimization. items.abstract: Abstract Background: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and stable coronary artery disease (SCAD) present overlapping clinical phenotypes, yet mandate divergent therapeutic strategies—urgent revascularization versus pharmacological optimization. Current diagnostic reliance on high-sensitivity cardiac troponin dynamic monitoring introduces hazardous delays (4–6 hours detection window) and yields false negatives in 20% of non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Pericoronary adipose tissue attenuation index (FAI), quantifying vascular inflammation through computed tomography (CT) attenuation changes in pericoronary fat, offers mechanistic insight into coronary plaque destabilization. However, the translational pathway from this biomarker to clinically actionable decision support remains incompletely realized, particularly regarding integration with established anatomical and functional parameters and explicit clinical interpretability. Hypothesis: A mechanistically grounded, multi-dimensional nomogram combining FAI with coronary CT angiography (CCTA)-derived anatomical stenosis (%DS), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and smoking status—rendered interpretable through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)—would achieve robust ACS-SCAD discrimination while providing transparent, auditable decision logic suitable for clinical implementation. Methods: In this prospective diagnostic accuracy study adhering to TRIPOD 2019 guidelines, 388 patients (ACS 117 [30.2%], SCAD 271 [69.8%]) underwent CCTA with standardized FAI, %DS, and LVEF acquisition. Stratified randomization (7:3) produced training (n=271) and validation (n=117) sets with preserved outcome distribution. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with 10-fold stratified cross-validation compared lambda.min versus lambda.1se selection criteria, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, Brier score, and decision curve analysis. KernelSHAP parsed individualized decision contributions. Regulatory-readiness was evaluated through predetermined change control documentation and explanation stability assessment. Results: LASSO lambda.min retained %DS, FAI, LVEF, RVEF, and smoking; lambda.1se selected only %DS and FAI. Final model incorporated %DS, FAI, LVEF, and smoking based on mechanistic non-overlap (RVEF-LVEF functional redundancy) and epidemiological importance. Multivariable analysis demonstrated %DS (OR 1.03, 95% CI: 1.01–1.04, P < 0.001) and FAI (OR 1.04, 95% CI: 1.02–1.06, P < 0.001) as positive ACS predictors; LVEF as protective (OR 0.96, 95% CI: 0.92–0.99, P = 0.032); smoking as marginally non-significant (OR 1.83, 95% CI: 0.87–3.86, P = 0.110) but incrementally contributory. Nomogram achieved AUC 0.86 (95% CI: 0.82–0.91) in training and 0.82 (95% CI: 0.75–0.90) in validation. Optimal cutoff 0.291 (Youden index) yielded training sensitivity 0.80, specificity 0.82, negative predictive value 0.91; validation sensitivity 0.73, specificity 0.72, negative predictive value 0.83. Calibration was satisfactory (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.347 and P = 0.405). Decision curve analysis demonstrated net benefit across threshold probability 0.10–0.55. SHAP analysis established a mechanistic hierarchy: %DS and FAI as dominant drivers (mean |SHAP| 0.75 and 0.70), LVEF as a functional protective modifier (0.35), and smoking as a behavioral risk stratifier (0.20). Individual force plots enabled case-level explanation with documented contribution stability. Conclusions: The %DS-FAI-LVEF-smoking nomogram achieves favorable ACS discriminatory accuracy with acceptable generalization. SHAP-enhanced interpretability satisfies emerging transparency requirements for artificial intelligence-enabled medical devices, supporting regulatory-ready clinical translation. Translational Significance: This study bridges the critical T1–T2 translational gap by converting perivascular inflammation biology (FAI) into an evidence-based diagnostic tool validated for a specific clinical decision context. The "one-stop" CCTA acquisition strategy—yielding anatomical, inflammatory, and functional data from a single examination—addresses implementation barriers in time-critical emergency settings. Explicit SHAP-based explainability exceeds current "black box" machine learning limitations, aligning with FDA and EMA guidance on predetermined change control and transparency documentation for clinical artificial intelligence. These design elements collectively reduce translational friction from research prototype to prospective clinical trials and eventual regulatory approval, advancing precision coronary care through mechanism-informed, transparently interpretable decision support.

items.abstract: Background: The microbiota–gut–brain axis provides an emerging framework for understanding neuropsychiatric disorders. Depression and addiction, despite substantial comorbidity, are frequently investigated separately. This review examines whether gut dysbiosis contributes to vulnerability, symptom persistence and recovery through shared inflammatory, endocrine, metabolic and reward-related mechanisms. Methods A structured narrative review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and PsycINFO, supplemented by citation searching. Priority was given to systematic reviews, meta-analyses, human cohorts, randomised trials and mechanistic studies. Evidence was evaluated for methodological quality, confounding, replication, biological plausibility and clinical relevance. Results Convergent evidence implicates altered short-chain fatty acid production, intestinal barrier dysfunction, dysregulated tryptophan–kynurenine metabolism, systemic inflammation, hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal-axis disturbance and altered affective and reward signalling. Human evidence is strongest for major depressive disorder and alcohol use disorder, whereas evidence involving opioids, psychostimulants, cannabis and polysubstance use remains comparatively limited. Dietary interventions, probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics and faecal microbiota transplantation demonstrate preliminary therapeutic potential. However, methodological heterogeneity, uncertain causality, limited replication and insufficient evidence of sustained benefit prevent routine clinical recommendation. Digital phenotyping, wearable technologies and artificial intelligence may facilitate integration of microbial, metabolic, behavioural and longitudinal clinical information, although prospective validation and demonstrated clinical utility remain limited. Conclusions The proposed Microbiota–Gut–Brain–Reward framework conceptualises dysbiosis as a potentially modifiable contributor rather than an independent cause of depression or addiction. Clinical translation requires longitudinal multi-omic research, harmonised methodologies, mechanistically informed trials and integration with established pharmacological, psychological and social interventions. Digitally enabled precision approaches may support personalised recovery monitoring, provided interpretability, privacy, equity and clinical governance are prioritised. The United Arab Emirates offers opportunities for culturally responsive translational research, although implementation must remain evidence-driven, ethically governed and subject to rigorous prospective evaluation before clinical adoption.

items.abstract: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by chronic cerebral hypoperfusion and cognitive decline, yet the role of fatty acid metabolism in its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Integrated transcriptomic profiling was combined with network-based analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning to uncover key fatty acid metabolism-associated molecular features associated with VaD. Single-cell RNA sequencing, intercellular communication inference, and in silico perturbation analyses were applied to define immune-stromal interactions. Potential therapeutic compounds were evaluated using molecular docking and dynamics simulations. We identified three VaD-related fatty acid metabolism genes (VaD-FAMRGs), namely PNPLA3, HSP90AA1, and ALB, which showed consistent diagnostic performance across multiple computational approaches and were associated with lipid metabolism, inflammatory processes, and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Functional enrichment, single-cell RNA sequencing, and in silico gene perturbation analyses provided exploratory insights into the potential associations of these candidate genes with lipid transport, metabolic regulation, synaptic maintenance, and immune-inflammatory processes. Cell-cell communication analysis further revealed activation of the ANGPTL signaling axis, suggesting impaired endothelial-glial interactions driven by lipid metabolic dysregulation. Regulatory network analysis identified key transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulators, including REST, miR-155-5p, and miR-21-5p, which may coordinately modulate VaD-FAMRG expression. Drug repurposing analysis highlighted quercetin as a candidate compound with predicted interactions with all three hub proteins, supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. These findings suggest that dysregulated fatty acid metabolism may be associated with the development and progression of VaD through coordinated metabolic, inflammatory, and neurovascular mechanisms. This study provides a systems-level framework for understanding the underlying pathological processes and establishes a theoretical basis for future mechanistic and experimental validation.

items.abstract: Recent advances in precision oncology fueled the development of nanotherapeutics,​ molecularly targeted drugs, engineered immunotherapies, RNA therapeutics, and smart biomaterials for more selective cancer treatment. However, long-term therapeutic responses remain restricted by interconnected adaptive mechanisms, including ABC transporter-mediated drug efflux, dysregulated signaling pathways, apoptosis evasion, immune escape, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and tumor microenvironment​ remodeling. In this review article, these processes are collectively framed as tumor-mediated molecular hijacking, describing malignant cell exploitation and microenvironmental pathways that promote multidrug resistance and therapeutic failure. The review critically examines nanotherapeutic and advanced biotherapeutic strategies to counteract these mechanisms, including functionalized nanocarriers, antibody-drug conjugates, CAR-T cells, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy, immune checkpoint blockade, mesenchymal stem-cell (MSC)-based therapeutics, CRISPR-mediated genome editing, bispecific T-cell engagers, and RNA-based approaches. Particular focus includes drug-delivery elements such as tumour penetration, intracellular trafficking, controlled release, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, and critical formulation attributes, as well as translational challenges such as manufacturability, scalability, reproducibility, stability, safety, and regulatory feasibility. Emerging biofabrication approaches enable the fabrication of adaptive and personalized delivery systems, while artificial intelligence and machine learning are utilized as tools for structure-guided design, nanocarrier optimization, treatment-response prediction, and patient-specific digital-twin modelling. This paper combines tumor-mediated molecular hijacking with drug delivery technology at the forefront and translational aspects to create a comprehensive platform for clinically relevant precision cancer therapeutics.Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

items.abstract: Machine learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) is an emerging paradigm of protein design where ML models trained on experimental data are used to guide exploration of a protein fitness landscape. Building an MLDE pipeline involves many design choices across the design-build-test-learn loop ranging from data collection strategies to modeling. The cost of collecting experimental data makes benchmarking every component of these pipelines prohibitively difficult, necessitating the development of synthetic landscapes. In this work, we develop a framework called SLIP ("Synthetic Landscape Inference for Proteins") for constructing synthetic landscapes with tunable difficulty based on Potts models. This framework can be extended to any protein family for which there is a sequence alignment. We show that our tuning framework provides landscapes sufficiently challenging to benchmark MLDE pipelines. SLIP is open-source and is available at https://github.com/google-research/slip.

items.abstract: The human gastrointestinal (GI) microbiota is a complex and dynamic microbial ecosystem that plays a fundamental role in maintaining host metabolism, immune homeostasis, intestinal barrier integrity, and protection against pathogenic microorganisms. Disruption of this microbial community, known as gut dysbiosis, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous GI and systemic diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), Clostridioides difficile infection, obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, colorectal cancer, and nonalcoholic fatty liver disease. Although antibiotics remain indispensable for the treatment of bacterial infections, their indiscriminate use frequently disrupts gut microbial composition, reduces microbial diversity, promotes opportunistic pathogen overgrowth, and accelerates the emergence of antimicrobial resistance. These limitations have stimulated increasing interest in microbiota-targeted interventions as safer and more sustainable therapeutic strategies. Probiotics and prebiotics have emerged as promising approaches for restoring gut microbial homeostasis through complementary mechanisms. Probiotics inhibit pathogen colonization, enhance intestinal barrier function, produce antimicrobial metabolites, and modulate host immune responses. Prebiotics selectively stimulate the growth and metabolic activity of beneficial microorganisms, promoting the production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) that support intestinal and systemic health. Increasing evidence from experimental studies, randomized clinical trials, and meta-analyses demonstrates that these microbiota-directed interventions can reduce antibiotic-associated diarrhea, improve symptoms of IBD and IBS, enhance Helicobacter pylori eradication, decrease recurrence of C. difficile infection, and contribute to the management of several metabolic disorders. Despite these promising findings, important challenges remain regarding strain specificity, optimal dosage, treatment duration, product standardization, regulatory oversight, and interindividual variability in treatment response. Emerging advances in metagenomics, metabolomics, artificial intelligence, and precision medicine are facilitating the development of personalized microbiome-based therapies that may further enhance clinical outcomes. This review critically summarizes the current understanding of GI microbiota dysbiosis, discusses the mechanisms through which probiotics and prebiotics restore microbial balance, evaluates their clinical applications as alternatives or adjuncts to antibiotic therapy, and highlights existing challenges and future research directions for microbiome-based therapeutics.

Differentiating neurodegenerative disorders like PD from non-neurodegenerative causes of parkinsonism can be challenging. In clinically uncertain parkinsonian syndrome (CUPS), dopamine transporter (DAT)-single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) can aid diagnosis. However, susceptibility map-weighted imaging (SMWI) provides a promising magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alternative. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy and reliability of visual SMWI assessment by radiologists in CUPS and the added value of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diagnostic software. Materials and methods Patients with CUPS who underwent DAT-SPECT between January 2019 and July 2023 were included. Four radiologists, blinded to clinical symptoms and diagnosis, visually rated nigrosome-1 on axial SMWI reconstructions as normal, unclear, or abnormal. After the initial assessment, the radiologists re-evaluated the scans with AI-driven software assistance, designed to classify and quantify nigrosome-1 integrity. The reference standard was the final clinical diagnosis incorporating DAT-SPECT results. Results One hundred eighty patients were included (mean age 67.9, range 31-86, 120 males), 84 with neurodegenerative and 96 with non-neurodegenerative parkinsonism. Mean diagnostic accuracy was 80% (range 73-83%), with substantial inter-rater reliability (Fleiss κ 0.65). With software assistance, diagnostic accuracy improved to 87% (range 85-91%), and inter-rater agreement increased to almost perfect (Fleiss κ 0.86). Conclusion SMWI, particularly with AI-driven software assistance, is a promising and accessible MRI-based technique that may support the diagnostic workup in clinically uncertain parkinsonism, aiding the distinction between neurodegenerative and non-neurodegenerative causes. Key points Question Can susceptibility map-weighted imaging (SMWI) reliably differentiate neurodegenerative from non-neurodegenerative parkinsonism in clinically uncertain cases, and does artificial intelligence (AI)-driven software assistance improve radiologist performance? Findings Visual assessment had an accuracy of 80%, with substantial inter-rater reliability. AI-driven software assistance increased accuracy to 87% and improved inter-rater reliability. Relevance statement SMWI can differentiate neurodegenerative from non-neurodegenerative parkinsonism in clinically uncertain cases and may support the diagnostic process by offering an accessible MRI-based technique, facilitating an efficient diagnostic workup, and enabling early diagnosis in clinically uncertain parkinsonism.

items.abstract: Background General practitioners face high complexity in clinical decision-making. Large language models (LLMs) may support clinical reasoning, but their impact on decision-making processes and postgraduate medical training remains unclear. This qualitative study aims to explore General Practice (GP) trainee's use of LLMs in clinical reasoning and their educational needs. Materials and methods GP trainees were recruited and interviewed with semi-structured interview-guide. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed qualitatively. Results Seventeen GP trainees participated (mean interview duration: 38 min; range: 21-63 min). AI was perceived as a tool to augment and accelerate clinical decision-making, while potential risks of deskilling were identified. Participants reported a lack of structured AI education and expressed a need for its integration into postgraduate training. Discussion Participants perceived AI primarily as a supportive tool that can complement clinical reasoning and improve access to medical knowledge. At the same time, they identified potential risks, including overreliance on AI-generated information and possible effects on the development of clinical expertise. These findings suggest that postgraduate medical training should address AI-related competencies, including critical appraisal, ethical responsibility and appropriate integration of AI into clinical decision-making. Conclusion AI is already part of clinical practice among GP trainees, offering opportunities to support learning and clinical reasoning while raising concerns about overreliance and critical appraisal. Postgraduate medical training in GP should therefore incorporate structured AI competencies to ensure responsible, reflective and patient-centered use of AI.

items.abstract: Clinical large language model (LLM) deployment is shifting from feasibility to liability, while current guidance largely treats model behavior as a control problem. We tested whether decision-style system prompts shift clinical action thresholds when clinical facts are held constant, and whether these shifts are consistent across settings and models. We defined nine physician personas by crossing three ethical orientations (duty-based, care-based, utilitarian) with three cognitive styles (intuitive, integrative, analytic). Twenty open-weight LLMs were evaluated on 2500 simulated emergency department vignettes and 2500 MIMIC-IV-Note discharge summaries. For each text, models answered five binary decision items (safety, autonomy, treatment, resource use, follow-up). Each condition was repeated ten times, yielding 5,000,000 total decisions. Under baseline prompting, models answered "Yes" to 42.8% of decisions. Persona prompts shifted affirmative rates from 36.9% to 46.4%, a 9.5 percentage-point swing under fixed clinical evidence. Effects were largest in autonomy and treatment and were consistent across corpora (85.7% directional agreement; r = 0.82 for effect sizes). Susceptibility varied by model (4.9-16.1 points), with no consistent protection from medical fine-tuning or model size. Decision-style system prompts reliably change clinical action thresholds in LLMs under fixed evidence. Prompting is a policy-setting layer, not just a communication layer, and should be treated as a first-class deployment configuration.

items.abstract: Background Late-onset sepsis (LOS) causes morbidity and mortality in very-low birthweight (VLBW) neonates. We previously developed a machine learning model, the Pulse Oximetry Warning System (POWS), to predict LOS in the next 24 h. The neonatal Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (nSOFA) score predicts sepsis mortality. We hypothesized that POWS scores would differentiate severe LOS events, defined by nSOFA >4, from milder events. Methods We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study including VLBW infants diagnosed with culture-confirmed LOS with continuous vital sign data available. Mixed-effects regression was used to examine the association between POWS and nSOFA. Results We analyzed 89 LOS episodes in 84 VLBW infants. Severe sepsis (nSOFA >4 within 48 h of blood culture) occurred in 27 (30%) episodes. Mean POWS scores were higher in the 24 h before severe LOS than non-severe LOS. POWS rose more steeply in the hours before sepsis diagnosis among infants with severe LOS. Conclusion POWS scores, predicting risk of LOS in the next 24 h, have a significantly higher rate of rise in severe episodes as compared to less severe episodes as measured by nSOFA. This result adds to evidence that POWS could prompt earlier intervention that improves sepsis outcomes. Impact Late-onset sepsis (LOS) is a leading cause of death and disability in premature infants. The Pulse Oximetry Warning System (POWS) uses continuous heart rate and oxygen saturation data to predict sepsis up to 24 h before clinical diagnosis. This study demonstrates that POWS rises more steeply before severe sepsis episodes, as defined by the neonatal Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (nSOFA) score, than before milder episodes. POWS thus may provide earlier warning of the most severe sepsis events, potentially enabling earlier intervention in this vulnerable population.

items.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) are widely used for noninvasive brain monitoring in clinical and cognitive applications, where machine learning-based classification has become increasingly prevalent. Alongside algorithmic advances, a growing body of literature reports signal-derived metrics as digital biomarkers; however, their interpretation, validity, and comparability remain strongly dependent on target definition, processing pipelines, and evaluation practices. This review provides a structured overview of EEG- and fNIRS-based classification studies, with a particular focus on signal processing workflows and biomarker extraction. The reviewed literature is organized around key stages of the analytical pipeline, including target formulation, data preprocessing, feature extraction, and validation. Common feature families-spanning spectral, temporal, connectivity-based, network-level, and hemodynamic representations-are summarized and discussed in relation to their typical applications and limitations. The main contribution is an evidence-based distinction between signal features and credible candidate biomarkers. Reliability, analytical robustness, external generalization, and interpretability are considered within the intended context of use. Clinical utility is assessed separately from predictive performance. Across 117 primary studies, most measures remained candidate biomarkers; only four studies were assigned to independent clinical validation, with qualifications, and none evaluated clinical utility.

items.abstract: Classifying viral pathogens from next-generation sequencing (NGS) data is central to diagnosis and genomic surveillance. Most deep learning classifiers, however, read only a fixed window at the start of each genome, typically a few hundred to a few thousand base pairs, and so ignore more than 95% of the sequence of large DNA viruses such as monkeypox virus (MPV) and herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1). We refer to this problem as Truncation Blindness. Here we present Viro-BERT, which splits a complete genome into overlapping 512-token windows, encodes each window with a shared DistilBERT encoder, and averages the window-level class probabilities in a Late Fusion Consensus layer. Because the windows are processed independently, memory use does not grow with genome length. We compared Viro-BERT with one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) and RoBERTa baselines on 14 viral classes, using the same segmentation and training protocol for all models. Viro-BERT reached 96.79% accuracy and a macro-F1 score of 96.17%. We then added random substitution noise to the test genomes. At 5% noise, the accuracy of the 1D-CNN fell by 5.57 percentage points, whereas Viro-BERT still classified 93.68% of genomes correctly. Positional and attention analyses on HSV-1 showed that Viro-BERT uses diagnostic signal from across the genome rather than from its 5' end alone. These results indicate that whole-genome context is needed for viral classifiers that remain reliable on noisy clinical data.

items.abstract: Background and objective Rapid growth in medical literature limits traditional systematic review methods, particularly in high-volume fields like maternity care. This paper presents a novel methodological approach using a hybrid workflow that combines Large Language Model (LLM) semantic data extraction with programmatic filtering to automate title and abstract screening. Methods The workflow was deployed on a high-volume clinical dataset (51,281 records retrieved from six databases) as a validation case study. Google Gemini 1.5-pro and 2.5-flash extracted 12 structured semantic variables, followed by a seven-stage rule-based filtering pipeline to determine eligibility. The workflow's accuracy was validated against a large-scale manual audit. Results The workflow reduced the human manual screening burden by 96%. Validation demonstrated an estimated sensitivity of 89.9% (95% confidence interval; CI 87.3-92.1%), specificity of 96.4% (95% CI 96.2-96.5%), and false negative rate of 0.18% (95% CI 0.09-0.35%), achieving accuracy comparable to dual-human review. Total API expenditure was US$458.73. Subgroup analysis found no change in screening accuracy after changing LLM. Discussion This approach offers a scalable, transparent, cost-effective, and model-agnostic solution for evidence synthesis. By decoupling data extraction from inclusion logic, researchers maintain granular control over eligibility criteria, supporting scalable evidence synthesis and living systematic reviews.

items.abstract: Background Machine learning (ML) methods may improve prediction of individual risk of mortality risk after congenital heart surgery (CHD) by identifying nonlinear relationships/novel combinations of variables. Improved risk discrimination may improve outcomes by optimizing resource allocation and patient surveillance. Methods Children and adolescents (age≤18 years) undergoing CHD surgery at Pediatric Cardiac Critical Care Consortium hospitals 9/1/2014-12/30/2019 were studied. Non-collinear potential predictors were identified empirically and used to create a logistic regression risk (LR) model (mimicking traditional risk-adjustment models) and ML (random forest and gradient boosting model) models. Model performance was evaluated using net reclassification index (NRI), the proportion of subjects in which either the absolute risk category or estimated risk relative to other subjects changed between each model and one composed only of STAT category as the primary outcome. This metric reflects how often a model changes how a clinician views the risk of a patient relative to a parsimonious model and provides some measure of the utility of these models. Secondary analyses compared overall model fit. Results In total 51,475 operative encounters from 52 hospitals were studied. Subjects were 45% female, 20% neonates, and 5% underwent STAT 5 operations. C-statistics and Brier scores did not differ significantly between ML and LR models. For absolute risk categorires, point estimates for NRI between ML-models and STAT category (0.76 95%CI: 0.68-0.83) suggested at best modest improvements compared to logistic regression model (0.75 95%CI 0.67-0.83), but the difference was not significant. Similarly, for rankings of risk within the cohort, NRI for ML models (0.26 95%CI: 0.19-0.32) was not significantly different to that for the LR model (0.24 95%CI: 0.17-0.33). Conclusion ML derived models did not improve overall model fit. Magnitude of improvement in reclassification was at best modest and not statistically significant. Future research is necessary to evaluate the added values of incorporating more comprehensive data and/or advanced computational techniques and use of reclassification in risk prediction.

items.abstract: Background Existing prediction models for stroke-heart syndrome (SHS) after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) have limited generalizability due to population heterogeneity. Objective To develop and validate a generalizable risk prediction model for SHS following AIS. Methods A retrospective cohort of 1404 AIS patients from the MIMIC-IV database was utilized. After feature selection, 14 machine learning algorithms were evaluated. All algorithms were trained under identical preprocessing with per-algorithm automatically tuned hyperparameters and evaluated by five-fold cross-validation and hold-out internal validation. The final model-a logistic regression-based nomogram-was externally validated on an independent single-center cohort (n = 321). Performance was assessed by discrimination (area under the curve [AUC]), calibration (calibration curves, Hosmer-Lemeshow test), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis). Model interpretability was augmented using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Results Seven early-admission predictors were identified: age, heart rate, prothrombin time, blood urea nitrogen, Glasgow Coma Scale score, respiratory rate, and body temperature. The model demonstrated strong, consistent discrimination across datasets: training AUC=0.789, internal validation AUC=0.802, and external validation AUC=0.810. Calibration was good on internal validation (Hosmer-Lemeshow P = 0.614) but showed external under-dispersion (slope 1.72, P = 0.004); local recalibration is indicated. Decision curve analysis confirmed clinical net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. Conclusion We developed and validated a parsimonious SHS risk prediction model using seven early-admission indicators that overcomes the generalizability limitations of prior tools through multi-algorithm validation and external testing. Relying on routine clinical variables, this tool facilitates rapid risk stratification for precision prevention, though future prospective validation in diverse populations is warranted.

items.abstract: Fatty acid composition is a major determinant of nutritional quality, oxidative stability and functional value of oilseed crops. It is shaped by coordinated plastidial fatty acid synthesis, endoplasmic reticulum-associated desaturation and elongation, acyl editing, triacylglycerol assembly and lipid turnover in seed. This review summarizes the metabolic basis of fatty acid diversity of edible oil in major and specialty oilseed crops, then examines how genetic architecture and omics-assisted discovery have accelerated the identification of loci, alleles and candidate genes controlling fatty acid composition. We emphasize a design framework that links locus discovery to allele prioritization, targeted editing, pathway engineering and field deployment. Linkage mapping, bulked segregant sequencing, genome wide association studies, transcriptomics, proteomics and pangenome analyses are increasingly revealing both canonical genes and previously unrecognized structural or regulatory variation. We further discuss improvement strategies ranging from conventional and marker-assisted breeding to single-gene editing, transgenic manipulation and multigene synthetic biology. Finally, we highlight emerging opportunities in population genomics, underutilized oil crop mining, artificial intelligence (AI)-guided enzyme and promoter design, and agronomic evaluation. Collectively, these advances are shifting oilseed improvement from empirical selection toward rational, pathway-informed design of fatty acid profiles, while emphasizing the continuing need for biochemical validation and field-level performance assessment.

items.abstract: Background Allergic rhinitis (AR) is characterized by a T helper 2 (Th2)-cell-mediated immune imbalance, yet its upstream molecular drivers remain poorly defined. Interleukin-17 receptor B (IL-17Rb) has been implicated in type 2 inflammation, but its precise functional role and mechanism in AR pathogenesis are unclear. Objective This study aimed to identify key immunoregulatory genes in AR via bioinformatics and to comprehensively elucidate the functional role and mechanisms of IL-17Rb using both in vivo animal and in vitro cellular models. Methods Candidate genes were screened using GEO datasets and machine learning. An HDM-induced AR murine model and in vitro cell models were utilized. AAV-mediated IL-17Rb knockdown or overexpression, alongside a specific STAT6 inhibitor (AS1517499), were employed. Evaluations included nasal symptoms, histopathology, STAT6 activation, and parameters of Th2 inflammation alongside the Th1/Th17/Treg balance (IL-4/5/13, IFN-γ, IL-17A, IL-10). Results Bioinformatics identified IL-17Rb as a pivotal upregulated gene in AR, correlating with Th2 infiltration (r = 0.74). In vivo, IL-17Rb knockdown alleviated AR symptoms, eosinophil/mast cell infiltration, and type 2 cytokine release. Importantly, it rectified the AR-associated immune imbalance by restoring IFN-γ (Th1) and IL-10 (Treg) while reducing IL-17A (Th17). Conversely, IL-17Rb overexpression exacerbated Th2 inflammation and STAT6 phosphorylation. Co-administration of AS1517499 successfully abrogated these overexpression-induced effects, confirming a STAT6-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, in vitro blockade of IL-17Rb inhibited IL-25-promoted Th2 differentiation and STAT6 activation. Conclusion IL-17Rb is a critical upstream immunoregulator in AR, driving STAT6-dependent Th2 inflammation and broadly modulating the Th1/Th17/Treg balance. Targeting the IL-17Rb/STAT6 axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy.

items.abstract: Purpose Cardiometabolic disease and obesity are important factors when considering breast cancer risk and survivorship. We aimed to utilize a fully automated deep learning algorithm to evaluate CT-derived cardiometabolic biomarkers in patients with breast cancer. Methods We applied fully automated deep learning algorithms to derive cardiometabolic markers from baseline computed tomography (CT) abdomen scans of females with breast cancer diagnosed between 2016 - 2018 at Johns Hopkins. Results Among 127 females (64.6% postmenopausal; 57.5% White and 26.8% Black race), BMI (body mass index) was positively correlated with CT-derived adipose tissue area and​ muscle area, and negatively correlated with liver intensity, but not associated with presence of aortic calcification. However, myosteatosis and menopausal status outperformed BMI as clinical markers of cardiometabolic health​ in breast cancer, as they were associated with both adiposity (especially visceral adiposity) and the presence of aortic calcification, with myosteatosis also being associated with liver steatosis. Conclusion Artificial intelligence algorithms can feasibly and directly quantify body composition, liver fat, and abdominal aortic plaque, and be a tool in evaluating metabolic disease risk in patients with breast cancer.

items.abstract: Purpose To assess the feasibility of personalized tumor-masked structural connectomics combined with interpretable machine learning (ML) for differentiating low-grade gliomas (LGG) from high-grade gliomas (HGG), and to identify candidate tract-specific connectomic biomarkers of glioma aggressiveness. Methods Thirty-five patients with histopathologically confirmed gliomas (20 LGG, 15 HGG) underwent preoperative diffusion tensor imaging and T1-weighted MRI. Tumor-masked probabilistic tractography was used to reconstruct individualized structural connectomes based on 50 white matter (WM) tract labels. We evaluated 296 graph-theoretical features using sequential feature selection and Random Forest classification within a strictly isolated nested cross-validation framework. We used SHAP analysis for model interpretation. Sensitivity analyses compared clinical-radiological, connectomic, and combined feature sets. Results The leak-free pure connectomics model achieved a mean ROC-AUC of 0.814 ± 0.327 (95% CI, 0.500-1.000), with a macro-F1 score of 0.786 ± 0.265. Restricting the analysis to non-zero connectomic features yielded a mean AUC of 0.833 ± 0.167. The clinical-radiological model achieved a mean AUC of 0.817 ± 0.149, while the combined clinical-radiological and connectomic model showed the highest point estimate (AUC, 0.933 ± 0.109; 95% CI, 0.798-1.068). SHAP analysis highlighted the sagittal stratum, medial lemniscus, and superior fronto-occipital fasciculus among the most informative WM pathways. Conclusion Tumor-masked structural connectomics combined with interpretable ML demonstrated preliminary feasibility for identifying candidate imaging biomarkers associated with glioma aggressiveness in neuroradiological practice. These findings are exploratory and represent internal estimates from a single cohort; external validation in independent, multi-center cohorts is required before any potential clinical application.

items.abstract: Objectives To develop radiomics model, 2D deep learning (2D DL) model, 2.5D deep learning (2.5D DL) model, 3D deep learning (3D DL) model, and their fusion models to differentiate spinal tuberculosis (STB) from spinal metastasis (SM) based on MR imaging. Methods This retrospective study included 186 STB patients and 219 SM patients. Patients from three hospitals were divided into a training set (n = 191), an internal test set (n = 82) and an external test set (n = 132). Using the ResNet50 network pre-trained leveraging the ImageNet dataset, we developed 2D, 2.5D, and 3D deep learning models based on MR imaging. We constructed the radiomics model by using PyRadiomics to extract radiomics features. Deep learning models and radiomics model were used to construct two fusion models: the feature-based model (Rad_DL_FB) and the decision-based model (Rad_DL_DB). And the accuracy of these models was validated. Results In the internal test set, the Rad_DL_FB model demonstrated superior performance compared to other models, achieving the highest AUC of 0.971 (95% CI: 0.953-0.989) and accuracy of 0.927. In the external test set, the Rad_DL_DB model demonstrated superior performance compared to other models, achieving the highest AUC of 0.961 (95% CI: 0.940-0.982) and accuracy of 0.909. Furthermore, fusion-model assistance significantly improved the diagnostic accuracy of junior spine surgeons and narrowed the observed performance gap between junior and senior surgeons. Conclusion The fusion models including Rad_DL_FB model and Rad_DL_DB model, which integrates radiomics features and deep learning features of different dimensions, can effectively differentiate STB from SM, thereby assisting clinicians in making clinical decisions.

items.abstract: Looped Transformers improve parameter efficiency by repeatedly applying the same Transformer layers. During autoregressive decoding, however, generating each token requires several sequential passes through these layers, leading to high decoding latency. Pipelined self-speculative methods use shallow-loop predictions to process tokens at different loops in the same batch, but each token must reach the drafting depth before the next can enter the pipeline. We introduce LoopFill, a training-free speculative decoding algorithm for looped LLM that combines multi-token suffix drafts with shallow-loop predictions in a single draft tree. Both drafters contribute to one tree, so a suffix lookup can immediately extend a shallow prediction and several future tokens can enter the pipeline together. The shared block computes the highest-scoring draft candidates at different loop depths in one batch, and full-depth verification preserves the model's autoregressive output distribution. Across seven benchmarks, LoopFill's average speedup over greedy autoregressive decoding is 5.85times on Ouro-2.6B and 5.13times on Huginn-3.5B. The speedups exceed those of LoopAhead, the strongest baseline, by \(40\%\) on Ouro-2.6B and \(25\%\) on Huginn-3.5B.

items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become central to neuro-oncological imaging, impacting clinical and scientific workflows. In clinical practice, AI-based image reconstruction and noise reduction expedite the generation of advanced multiparametric MRI and PET scans. Automated segmentation and volumetric analysis improve reproducibility, speed, and standardization of tumor quantification and response assessment. In research, large language and multimodal models extract structured information from radiology reports and medical records. Collaborative initiatives, such as BraTS and FeTS, have established standardized, privacy-compliant frameworks for large-scale quantitative analyses. Tumor-specific applications include noninvasive molecular profiling in gliomas, grading and recurrence prediction in meningiomas, detection and response assessment in brain metastases, and pediatric-specific modeling aligned with RAPNO. However, AI models remain sensitive to technical and biological variations across institutions, limiting their clinical utility unless appropriate training and validation is performed. Nevertheless, progress is evident in prospective, biopsy-validated infiltration mapping, assessment of resection extent aligned with RANO-Resect, and standardization through AI-RANO. Emerging directions include foundation models, uncertainty estimation, federated learning, AI-enhanced ultra-low-field MRI, and dual-tracer PET. When used as a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for the imaging team, AI can increasingly improve the utility, reproducibility, and efficiency of quantitative, multiparametric imaging in patients with brain tumors.
